item.title: Longitudinal viral load trajectories predict cervical lesion risk in women with persistent human papillomavirus infection: A prospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
item.description:
Authors: Zhou Y, Chen S, Zhang Y, Jiang Y, Xiao M, Xin X, Shi Z, Zhang L
Journal: Cancer | DOI: 10.1002/cncr.70648
Published: 2026-Dec-01
PMID: 43069728



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is central to cervical lesion development, but single viral-load measurements may not capture heterogeneous viral dynamics. This study characterized longitudinal viral-load trajectories among women with persistent infection and evaluated their associations with cervical lesions and incremental predictive value beyond baseline factors. METHODS: In this prospective cohort of 1502 HPV-positive women followed at approximately 6-month intervals, latent class growth analysis using actual follow-up time was conducted among 624 women with type-specific persistent infection. Associations between trajectory group and any cervical lesion (low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion [HSIL]) were assessed using multivariable logistic regression; HSIL was explored using Firth-penalized regression. Discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve analysis were used to assess incremental predictive performance. RESULTS: Of 1170 women with classifiable outcomes, 624 had persistent infection. Four trajectories were identified: low stable (39.6%), moderate declining (18.9%), moderate increasing (29.8%), and persistently high (11.7%). Any-lesion prevalence was 10.9%, 17.8%, 74.2%, and 90.4%, respectively (p < .001). Compared with the low-stable group, fully adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were 1.95 (95% CI, 1.02-3.74), 29.66 (95% CI, 16.75-52.51), and 124.29 (95% CI, 47.30-326.60) for the other groups, respectively. The persistently high group was also associated with HSIL (OR, 9.47; 95% CI, 3.18-33.09). The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) increased from 0.713 for the base model to 0.888 for both the simple longitudinal and trajectory models and 0.899 for the joint model. CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal HPV viral-load dynamics identified clinically distinct risk phenotypes. Moderate-increasing and persistently high trajectories were strongly associated with cervical lesions, whereas longitudinal information improved discrimination beyond baseline measurements. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

item.title: Outcome of Surgical Interventions for Deep Interarytenoid Notch in Paediatrics: A Systematic Review.
item.dc:creator: Saniasiaya J, van der Meer G
item.description:
Authors: Saniasiaya J, van der Meer G
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261508792
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43094457



Abstract:
UNLABELLED: Deep interarytenoid notch (DIN), a subclassification of type 1 laryngeal cleft (LC) has been found to cause dysphagia and aspiration in children, necessitating long-term feeding assistance. Various surgical interventions have shown promising results, although the outcomes and complications remain unknown. OBJECTIVE: We aim to investigate the outcome of surgical interventions for DIN in children. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus databases were searched from inception to May 31, 2025. RESULTS: Five studies were identified, involving a total of 117 children with a mean age of 22.4 months. DIN was diagnosed following an airway and swallowing assessment. All included children were trialled with feeding therapy before surgical interventions. Interarytenoid injection laryngoplasty (IL) was the favoured technique in 98.3% of included children. A statistically significant improvement in post-surgical interventions was observed across the included studies. 7.7% reported persistent symptoms requiring endoscopic surgical repair. No major or minor complications were reported. CONCLUSION: Surgical interventions, notably interarytenoid IL, demonstrated significant improvement and resolution of symptoms; early surgical interventions in children with DIN may improve dysphagia, alleviating the need for assisted feeding. Yet, multicentre, large, prospective, controlled trials comparing various treatment modalities are imperative to determine the efficacy of interventions for DIN in children.

item.title: Reducing the Rates of Operating Room Intervention for Pharyngeal Foreign Bodies.
item.dc:creator: Danis DO, Dalal K, Siegel R, Buffington K, Bharathi R, O'Leary M, Scott AR
item.description:
Authors: Danis DO, Dalal K, Siegel R, Buffington K, Bharathi R, O'Leary M, Scott AR
Journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology | DOI: 10.1177/00034894261509205
Published: 2026-Nov-26
PMID: 43094453



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study presents a case series of patients who presented to the emergency department with pharyngeal foreign bodies and describes the success rate of awake removal in a clinic setting using topical anesthetic and flexible fiberoptic laryngoscopy (FFL). METHODS: Case series with retrospective chart review. The billing database of an urban, academic, tertiary otolaryngology clinic was queried to identify patients presenting for evaluation of odynophagia from suspect upper aerodigestive foreign body. All patients with visualized foreign body were managed with an identical technique for bedside removal. RESULTS: From 2020 to 2026, 36 cases (25 female, 11 male) were evaluated for pharyngeal foreign body and underwent bedside removal attempts using a 2-person approach, where 1 operator performs FFL, while another manually retracts the tongue, and uses curved Kelly Forceps to remove the foreign body. Foreign bodies consisted of a fishbone (0.2-3 cm) in 35 cases and a metal bristle in 1 case. The most common foreign body location was in the tongue base/vallecula in 26 cases (72%). Common presenting symptoms were odynophagia, throat discomfort, and foreign body sensation. 29/30 (97%) of adult cases had successful bedside removal. In 1 failed attempt, the patient swallowed the foreign body prior to removal. Only 2 pediatric cases (4 and 7 years) had successful bedside removal, whereas 3 pediatric cases (19 months-8 years) failed awake attempts at removal. CONCLUSION: Pharyngeal foreign bodies require timely removal given risk for serious complications. We found that the curvature of Kelly forceps is suitable in awake and upright patients. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV.

item.title: TTF-1 and PD-L1 interplay as prognostic biomarkers in first-line metastatic lung adenocarcinoma: a multicentre real-world study.
item.dc:creator: Maffezzoli M, Monaca F, Cantale O, Gomez-Randulfe I, Teoh A, Htun L, Gregory M, Holden C, Oludipe M, Mawella R, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Maffezzoli M, Monaca F, Cantale O, Gomez-Randulfe I, Teoh A, Htun L, Gregory M, Holden C, Oludipe M, Mawella R, et al.
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag469
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43094069



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1) is routinely assessed in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) as a diagnostic marker. Evidence suggests that TTF-1 may also have prognostic relevance in metastatic NSCLC (aNSCLC). We investigated the prognostic impact of TTF-1 expression in aNSCLC receiving first-line immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy and its interplay with PD-L1. METHODS: This was a multicentre retrospective real-world study including patients with aNSCLC treated at five UK institutions with first-line ICI monotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy (CT+ICI) between 2017 and 2025. Outcomes were analysed according to TTF-1 status and PD-L1 expression, primarily in patients with adenocarcinoma (ADK). Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) was included as an exploratory comparator. RESULTS: Among 823 patients, 288 (35.0%) were TTF-1 negative (TTF1-) and 535 (65.0%) TTF-1 positive (TTF1+). TTF1- tumours included ADK (121, 42.0%) and SCC (167, 58.0%). TTF1-/ADK had shorter PFS (5.79 vs 9.90 months, HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.25-1.93, p < 0.001) and OS (11.12 vs 19.08 months, HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.26-1.98, p < 0.001) than TTF1+/ADK. Exploratory comparisons showed that TTF1-/SCC had poorer outcomes than TTF1+/ADK, although not different compared to TTF1-/ADK. In multivariable analyses focused on ADK, TTF-1 positivity remained independently associated with improved PFS (p=0.001) and OS (p<0.001). The prognostic association of TTF-1 was most pronounced in the PD-L1 1-49% subgroup and interaction testing confirmed significant heterogeneity between PD-L1 < 1% and 1-49%. CONCLUSIONS: TTF1-/ADK showed worse outcomes, with the strongest prognostic association in the PD-L1 1-49% subgroup. These findings support further investigation of prognostic heterogeneity and require independent validation.

item.title: Characterization and Role of Radiotherapy in Chinese Patients with Nuclear Protein in Testis (NUT) Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Xu L, Ai X, Liu S, Quan T, Shen J, Yang Y, Chen Z, Mao YP, Sun Y, Zhou G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Xu L, Ai X, Liu S, Quan T, Shen J, Yang Y, Chen Z, Mao YP, Sun Y, Zhou G, et al.
Journal: The oncologist | DOI: 10.1093/oncolo/oyag461
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43094055



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nuclear protein in testis carcinoma (NUTC) is a rare and aggressive malignancy driven by NUTM1 rearrangement. While previous studies have focused on Western populations, data on Chinese NUTC remain scarce. METHODS: We screened 1,012 medical records from a single cancer center's intelligence platform. Chinese patients with pathologically confirmed NUTC were included. The clinicopathological characteristics of Chinese NUTC were compared with that of Western population. Cox regression model was performed to identify variables associated with survival outcomes. RESULTS: Between 2017-2023, 68 Chinese patients who met the eligible criteria were enrolled. The median age was 40.5 years (range, 1-79), which is older than the reported from Western patients in the NUT Midline Carcinoma Registry. 41 (60.3%) Chinese patients had head and neck origin compared to the thoracic-dominant origin in Western NUTC (P =0.02). After a median follow-up of 36.3 months, median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) times of the whole cohort were 7.1 (95%CI: 5.1-9.1) and 11.8 (95%CI: 9.2-14.5) months, respectively. Further analysis revealed that patients with tumors of head and neck region had significantly better survival than that of thoracic region (Hazard ratio =1.81, P =0.04). Other prognostic factors included tumor size, lymph node and/or organ metastasis at diagnosis, expression level of Ki-67. For treatment-related factors, in addition to the reception of surgery, administration of radiotherapy was also an essential prognostic factor (Hazard ratio =0.22, P <0.01) . CONCLUSION: This study outlines distinct clinicopathological features of Chinese NUTC, and highlights radiotherapy as an effective treatment for NUTC.

item.title: Outcomes of Operative Versus Nonoperative Treatment of T4 Oropharyngeal SCC: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Finnegan E, Olson BG, Moore EJ
item.description:
Authors: Finnegan E, Olson BG, Moore EJ
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70551
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43085959



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The incidence of oropharyngeal carcinoma (OPSCC) has increased in recent decades. T4 staging in OPSCC remains a poor prognostic factor, with the optimal treatment for T4 OPSCC unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare primary operative and nonoperative treatment in patients with T4 OPSCC. METHODS: Searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Cochrane Library through September 2024. Studies comparing primary operative with nonoperative management for T4 OPSCC were included. Random effect models generated pooled risk ratios and hazard ratios. RESULTS: Five non-randomized cohort studies involving 10 158 patients were included, largely comprised of patients with resectable T4a disease. Of these, 23% (n = 2333) received operative management, and 77% (n = 7405) received nonoperative management. Operative management was associated with improved overall survival (OS) (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.41-0.80; p = 0.001), disease-specific survival (DSS) (HR 0.44; 95% CI 0.31-0.74; p = 0.001), and disease-free survival (DFS) (HR 0.48; 95% CI 0.26-0.72; p = 0.001). No significant differences in overall recurrence rates were found. Subgroup analysis showed reduced recurrence for p16-positive patients receiving surgery. Functional outcomes and complications were similar between surgical and nonoperative management groups. CONCLUSION: This study supports a potential association between operative management and improved OS, DSS, and DFS in patients with T4 OPSCC. Among patients with p16-positive tumors, operative treatment appeared to be associated with lower observed recurrence rates, while no difference in recurrence was observed in the overall cohort. Further high-quality evidence is needed to confirm these findings and inform treatment planning.

item.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis.
item.dc:creator: Anderson NC, Berth SH
item.description:
Authors: Anderson NC, Berth SH
Journal: BMJ (Clinical research ed.) | DOI: 10.1136/bmj-2026-085090
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43085813



Abstract:
Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

item.title: Comparing paclitaxel plus cisplatin versus cisplatin in concurrent chemoradiotherapy for stage IV locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a phase II randomized trial.
item.dc:creator: Lu ZJ, Yang Q, Yang ZC, Chen QY, Liu LT, Sun R, Mo HY, Luo DH, Liu SL, Guo SS, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Lu ZJ, Yang Q, Yang ZC, Chen QY, Liu LT, Sun R, Mo HY, Luo DH, Liu SL, Guo SS, et al.
Journal: ESMO open | DOI: 10.1016/j.esmoop.2026.108610
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43085179



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with stage IV locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC) remain at high risk of recurrence and distant metastasis despite intensity-modulated radiotherapy and concurrent cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Paclitaxel plus platinum (TP) has yielded encouraging activity. This randomized, open-label phase II trial evaluated whether concurrent TP could improve progression-free survival (PFS) compared with standard high-dose cisplatin (DDP) during chemoradiotherapy. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with stage IV LA-NPC were randomly assigned 1 : 1 to concurrent TP (paclitaxel plus cisplatin every 4 weeks for two cycles; planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose, 160 mg/m2) or DDP (cisplatin every 3 weeks for three cycles; planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose, 300 mg/m2) during chemoradiotherapy. The primary endpoint was 3-year PFS in the intention-to-treat population. RESULTS: Between February 2017 and September 2019, 184 patients were enrolled (92 patients per group). Median follow-up was 47.6 months. The 3-year PFS rates were 68.2% [95% confidence interval (CI) 58.6-77.8] with TP and 72.8% (95% CI 63.8-81.8) with DDP [stratified hazard ratio (HR) 1.16, 95% CI 0.71-1.90, Plog-rank = 0.56]. The stratified HR for overall survival (OS) was 0.38 (95% CI 0.13-1.09, P = 0.07). Given the limited number of deaths, no OS advantage of TP can be concluded. The cumulative incidence of locoregional relapse and distant metastasis did not differ between groups. The DDP group had higher rates of any-grade nausea, vomiting, anorexia, constipation, and thrombocytopenia (all P < 0.05), whereas grade 3-4 neutropenia was numerically higher with TP (22.0% versus 13.5%, P = 0.14). Late toxicities did not differ significantly (all P ≥ 0.12). CONCLUSIONS: With a lower planned cumulative concurrent cisplatin dose in the TP arm, TP did not demonstrate an improvement in PFS compared with standard DDP in concurrent chemoradiotherapy for stage IV LA-NPC. These findings do not support replacing standard DDP with this reduced-cisplatin TP schedule and do not exclude a potential benefit of adding paclitaxel to an equivalent-dose cisplatin backbone.

item.title: Prenatal developmental toxicity of the 70% ethanolic extract of defatted Lepidium sativum L. seeds in Wistar rats.
item.dc:creator: Aragie TG, Asres K, Ergete W, Woldekidan S, Abebe A, Sisay B, Seyoum G
item.description:
Authors: Aragie TG, Asres K, Ergete W, Woldekidan S, Abebe A, Sisay B, Seyoum G
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0363832
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43084588



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lepidium sativum Linn. seeds are widely consumed for medicinal and nutritional purposes, including among pregnant women; however, its safety profile during gestation remains inadequately defined. Therefore, this study evaluated the prenatal developmental toxicity of Lepidium sativum seeds in rats. METHODS: A total of five groups of pregnant Wistar rats were employed to evaluate the prenatal developmental effects of Lepidium sativum seed extract in two independent experimental arms. Treatments were administered via oral gavage during critical period of organogenesis (gestational day 12 [GD12] with the aim to evaluate the extract's effect on embryonic development. In GD12 experiment, each group containing a specific number of rats: group I and V consisted of ten rats each, while groups II, III, and IV included nine rats per group. Separate cohorts were examined on GD20 to capture near term developmental outcomes and late-stage developmental effects of the extract. The number of pregnant rats available for GD20 subgroup was ten in groups I, IV, and V, nine in group II, and seven in group III respectively. In both studies, groups I- III served as experimental groups and were given 250 mg/kg, 500 mg/kg, and 1000 mg/kg of the extract respectively during GD6-12. While, groups IV and V were pair-fed and ad libitum controls respectively. One-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc test was used to compare the groups, and statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05. RESULTS: In the GD12 subgroup, embryos from 1000 mg/kg of the extract exhibited significantly lower morphological scores in the embryonic heart (p < 0.01), otic (p = 0.002), and olfactory (p = 0.004) systems. A higher incidence of stillbirths and low birthweight pups was observed in 1000 mg/kg treated rats of GD20. Additionally, brain ventricular dilation was observed in 8% of fetuses from groups treated with 1000 mg/kg compared to the controls (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Oral administration of Lepidium sativum seed extract during gestational day 6-12 at 500 mg/kg and 1000 mg/kg doses was associated with significant developmental delays in rat embryos. The extract also resulted in a higher number of stillbirths, low birthweight, and developmental delays in rat fetuses.

item.title: Effects of hypochlorous acid and sodium hypochlorite irrigation protocols, used alone or combined with ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, on root canal dentin: An in vitro study.
item.dc:creator: Simo N, Paredes A, Villanueva Á, Ghilotti J, Llena C
item.description:
Authors: Simo N, Paredes A, Villanueva Á, Ghilotti J, Llena C
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0363657
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43084564



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This in vitro study evaluated the effect of irrigation protocols based on 5.25% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) or 200 ppm hypochlorous acid (HOCl), used alone or combined with 17% ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), on smear layer removal, open dentinal tubules and erosion of root canal dentin. METHODS: Forty-five palatal or distal roots of human molars were instrumented to size 50/.06 and randomly allocated to NaOCl + EDTA, NaOCl, HOCl + EDTA or HOCl (n = 10 each) or to a saline negative control (n = 5). Canals received 2 mL of irrigant after each instrument and a final sequence with 3 mL of each solution for 20 s. Root thirds were examined by scanning electron microscopy. A trained, calibrated and blinded examiner (weighted κ = 0.88) scored smear layer and erosion on ordinal scales; open tubules were quantified by digital image segmentation. RESULTS: Smear layer scores differed among groups only in the middle third (p = 0.013), where NaOCl + EDTA left less smear layer than NaOCl alone (p = 0.008); HOCl + EDTA did not differ significantly from HOCl alone or from NaOCl + EDTA in any third. In both combined protocols smear layer was greatest apically (p < 0.001). Images completely covered by smear layer could not be segmented, so open tubules were quantified in only 20-23 of 45 specimens per third, without significant differences between the combined protocols. Erosion was assessable in only 28 of 135 images and was reported descriptively. CONCLUSIONS: With syringe irrigation, neither chlorine-based irrigant removed the smear layer without a chelator. EDTA significantly reduced smear layer with 5.25% NaOCl, but no significant contribution was detected with 200 ppm HOCl in this sample. These findings do not support replacing NaOCl with HOCl and agree with existing evidence supporting NaOCl followed by EDTA as the reference protocol.

item.title: Network toxicology and molecular docking identify candidate molecular links between bis (1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Liu Z, Fan H, Li D, He Y, Yin J, Gu Y
item.description:
Authors: Liu Z, Fan H, Li D, He Y, Yin J, Gu Y
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0363655
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43084515



Abstract:
Bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (BDCIPP), a major metabolite and urinary biomarker of tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TDCIPP), has recently been associated with an increased risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC); however, the molecular basis of this association remains poorly understood. This study integrated in silico toxicity profiling, network toxicology, functional enrichment analysis, and molecular docking to investigate the potential molecular links between BDCIPP and ESCC. BDCIPP-related targets were collected from TargetNet, SwissTargetPrediction, STITCH, and CTD, whereas ESCC-related targets were obtained from GeneCards, OMIM, and TTD. Intersecting the two target sets yielded 102 common targets, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis prioritized 10 candidate hub targets, including EGFR, CASP3, CTNNB1, MYC, ESR1, MMP9, SRC, PTGS2, ERBB2, and SIRT1. Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis highlighted apoptosis-related regulation and extracellular matrix disassembly, whereas Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed enrichment of cancer-related pathways, including ErbB, PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and focal adhesion, as well as inflammatory and chemical carcinogenesis-related pathways. Molecular docking indicated varying degrees of predicted structural compatibility between BDCIPP and the candidate hub proteins, with ERBB2 exhibiting the lowest top-ranked MOE docking score among the examined proteins. Cross-method integration further highlighted EGFR/ERBB2-centered signaling, MMP9-associated extracellular matrix remodeling, PTGS2-related inflammatory regulation, and CASP3/SIRT1-mediated apoptotic control as candidate mechanistic modules. By focusing specifically on BDCIPP rather than extrapolating mechanistic evidence from its parent compound TDCIPP, these findings delineate a systems-level molecular framework potentially linking BDCIPP to ESCC and provide prioritized, experimentally testable targets and pathways for subsequent exposure-informed validation.

item.title: Cervical Lymph Node Management and Immune Checkpoint Inhibition in Mucosal Head and Neck Cancer.
item.dc:creator: Wu SS, Jetly A, Sunwoo JB, Holsinger FC, Colevas AD, Beadle B, Lee JJ, Finegersh A, Chen MM, Baik FM, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Wu SS, Jetly A, Sunwoo JB, Holsinger FC, Colevas AD, Beadle B, Lee JJ, Finegersh A, Chen MM, Baik FM, et al.
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3698
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43084321



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cervical lymph node basins may serve as sites of antitumor immune activation during immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) therapy. However, the impact of prior neck dissection (ND) or radiation therapy (RT) on survival outcomes in the setting of ICI is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between prior neck treatment and survival outcomes in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) treated with ICI. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Patients aged 18 years or older with mucosal HNSCC treated at a tertiary-level, academic institution between January 1, 2015, and July 31, 2025, were included in this cohort study. Cox proportional hazards models were performed. Kaplan-Meier method modeled overall survival (OS). EXPOSURE: ICI treatment. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcome was OS, measured as time between the first cycle of ICI and date of death or date of last follow-up. RESULTS: Of 336 patients (median [IQR] age, 68.0 [59.1-76.9] years; 243 [72.3%] male; 167 [49.7%] current or former smokers), primary tumor site was oral cavity in 128 (38.1%), oropharynx in 110 (32.7%), nasopharynx or sinonasal in 47 (14.0%), larynx or hypopharynx in 31 (9.2%), and salivary in 20 (6.0%). Pembrolizumab was the most common ICI agent. Treatments before ICI included RT in 240 patients (71.4%), chemotherapy in 193 (57.4%), surgical resection in 199 (59.2%), and ND in 149 (44.3%). On unadjusted Kaplan-Meier analysis, patients with ND had worse OS compared with those without ND (hazard ratio [HR], 1.41; 95% CI, 1.07-1.86). Among patients with prior ND, total lymph node count did not correlate with OS. OS was not different based on prior RT or chemotherapy. Prior ND was associated with worse OS in tumors with a combined positive score (CPS) of 1 or greater (HR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.07-2.28). Oropharyngeal cancers were the only tumor site to have worse OS with prior ND (HR, 1.75; 95% CI, 1.07-2.87). On multivariable analysis, earlier treatment period (adjusted HR [AHR], 1.45; 95% CI, 1.07-1.96), worse Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status Scale score (AHR, 2.79; 95% CI, 1.91-4.06), and CPS below 1 (AHR, 2.62; 95% CI, 1.55-4.45) were associated with worse OS; however, prior ND was not. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, patients with HNSCC who had ND before ICI had worse OS, but prior ND was not independently associated with OS after adjusting for other clinicopathologic factors. Prior ND was independently associated with worse OS in the oropharyngeal cohort. Future studies are needed to establish the impact of comprehensive lymphadenectomy on ICI efficacy.

item.title: Exercise Prehabilitation and Recovery After Head and Neck Cancer Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
item.dc:creator: Bhatnagar K, Krippaehne E, McGeachy W, Schultz A, Barber M, Rakshe S, Ye S, Lim JY, Pelz KR, Bartho M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bhatnagar K, Krippaehne E, McGeachy W, Schultz A, Barber M, Rakshe S, Ye S, Lim JY, Pelz KR, Bartho M, et al.
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3673
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43084284



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Preoperative physical activity is associated with improved postoperative outcomes in various cancer populations, but its impact for patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) remains understudied. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of an exercise prehabilitation program on postoperative mobility after HNC surgery. DESIGN, SETTINGS, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized clinical trial conducted from January 2024 to December 2025 at a single tertiary center in Portland, Oregon, included adults undergoing HNC surgery with free flap reconstruction. Patients with planned postoperative intensive care unit stays, severe mental health conditions, serious heart or lung conditions, bony metastases, falls within the past year, cognitive impairments, or impaired mobility requiring assistive devices were excluded. Follow-up was through hospital discharge or postoperative day 14. INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized to 2 to 5 weeks of exercise prehabilitation or control. Prehabilitation involved walking 2000 to 4000 steps per day, measured using wearable activity trackers, and strength exercises 3 times weekly. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was daily postoperative step counts. Secondary outcomes included postoperative complications, length of stay, discharge disposition, pain scores, and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality-of-Life Questionnaire, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 for depression, and program satisfaction surveys. RESULTS: A total of 52 patients were randomized (25 control, 27 intervention); 12 discontinued after randomization, leaving 40 patients (median [IQR] age, 61 [53-68] years; 25 [63%] male) for analysis (20 per group). Twenty-five participants (63%) had oral cavity or oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Lower extremity flaps were received in 8 patients (40%) in the prehabilitation group and 12 patients (60%) in the control group (standardized mean difference [SMD], 0.41). Baseline comorbidities, cancer characteristics, sarcopenia, functional performance, and wearable activity tracker adherence were comparable. Median (IQR) preoperative step counts were similar (4950 [3330-7370] steps for prehabilitation vs 4730 [4040-6650] steps for control; SMD = 0.07). There were no differences in postoperative step counts or secondary outcomes. In an exploratory analysis, patients above the median preoperative steps (4810) demonstrated greater postoperative mobility (median [IQR] of 1150 [332-1840] steps for those above the median vs 335 [81-491] steps for those below the median; log-transformed difference, 1.39 [95% CI, 0.49-2.30]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this randomized clinical trial demonstrate that exercise prehabilitation was feasible for patients with HNC but did not generate significant improvements in early postoperative outcomes. Abstract:
BACKGROUND: National statistics aggregate Hispanic/Latino individuals, potentially masking differences in health outcomes. METHODS: Data were obtained from the National Cancer Institute mortality database with detailed Hispanic/Latino origin (Mexican, Puerto Rican, Cuban, and other Hispanic/Latino) for all states and DC (2003-2023). item.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Dry Mouth/Sicca Symptoms and Sjögren-Spectrum Toxicity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Reported Incidence.

item.description:
Authors: Izzetti R, Cinquini C, Barone A, Nisi M
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70521
Published: 2026-Nov-25
PMID: 43081690



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the proportion of ICI-treated patients developing dry mouth/sicca symptoms, and to synthesize the evidence on clinical and serologic features of this condition. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched up to April 2026. Studies reporting data on sicca syndrome, xerostomia, sialadenitis, or Sjögren-spectrum toxicity in ICI-treated patients were included. Studies with an extractable denominator were included in the meta-analysis. Studies without a denominator were retained for descriptive synthesis. Risk-of-bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool for the denominator-based studies and the Joanna Briggs Institute checklists for case reports and case series. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies met eligibility criteria. Five studies (516 ICI-treated patients; 40 events) were included in the meta-analysis, giving an 8.7% (95% CI, 5.1%-14.3%) proportion of reported dry mouth/sicca symptoms of any severity, with moderate-to-substantial between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 65.5%, 95% CI 9.9%-86.8%). item.title: Impact of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Head and Neck Cancer: Integrated Evidence From TCGA Genomic Analysis and a US Multicenter Database Study.

item.description:
Authors: Chen TY, Jin L, Mao PC, Chou CW, Chen HY, Chang R, Li CJ, Liu WS
Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70805
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43079591



Abstract:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a risk factor for head and neck cancer (HNC), but the effects of antidiabetic drugs on this risk are unclear. We evaluated glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) using the TriNetX US electronic health record database, while investigating the molecular role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) in HNC. Adults ≥ 40 years with newly diagnosed T2DM (2012-2024) were studied retrospectively. Among > 250 million records, 105,605 GLP-1RA users were propensity-score matched 1:1 with 105,605 nonusers. Over a median 5-year follow-up, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower risks of incident HNC (HR: 0.723; 95% CI: 0.617-0.848) and all-cause mortality (HR: 0.737; 95% CI: 0.715-0.759). Molecular analyses showed that higher GLP1R expression was associated with better overall survival in The Cancer Genome Atlas Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-HNSC). In an independent multi-institutional biobank (Tri-VGH Biobank), GLP1R expression was significantly lower in tumor than matched adjacent non-tumor tissues (27 pairs), findings confirmed by tumor immunofluorescence. Overall, these epidemiological and molecular findings support a potential protective role of GLP-1RA/GLP1R signaling in HNC.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We present our experience with open total cricoid ring resection/partial laryngectomy with free flap reconstruction in the setting of cricoid chondrosarcoma. METHODS: Retrospective chart review of patients undergoing open total cricoid ring resection/partial laryngectomy for low to moderate grade cricoid chondrosarcoma. All patients were reconstructed with an autologous rib, wrapped with vascularized fascia harvested from an anterolateral thigh free flap. item.title: Antibody-Drug Conjugates and Oral Toxicities.
item.dc:creator: Nagarajan N, Brondfield S, Qureshi K, Villa A

Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70530
Published: 2026-Nov-24
PMID: 43078522



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are an emerging and promising class of anticancer therapeutics. This retrospective study aimed to characterize the oral toxicities associated with ADC treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted using de-identified clinical data from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) PatientExploreR database through 2024. A total of 13 ADCs were included in the analysis. Demographic characteristics, cancer diagnoses, treatment data, and oral toxicity data were retrieved for all eligible patients. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Descriptive statistics summarized demographic characteristics, smoking status, oral toxicity prevalence, and median time to onset. Associations between oral toxicity categories and sex, race, and smoking status were assessed using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests. RESULTS: A total of 1144 patients who received ADC therapy were included in the study, including 59.7% females, 15.9% males, and 24.0% unknown. Oral toxicities were recorded in 13.7% of patients, with mucosal lesions being the most prevalent (10.5%), followed by dry mouth (2.3%) and orofacial neuropathies (1.0%). A Pearson's chi-square test demonstrated a significant association between sex at birth and oral toxicity category (p = 0.023). The frequency of oral mucosal lesions varied significantly across the ADCs (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test with Monte Carlo simulation, 100 000 replicates; p < 0.0001). The frequency of dry mouth and orofacial neuropathies did not differ significantly among the ADCs (p = 0.412 and 0.297). CONCLUSION: Given the expanding use of ADCs in cancer therapy, characterization of their toxicity profile is essential. In this study, oral toxicities were observed in 13.7% of patients, with oral mucosal lesions being the predominant toxicity, followed by dry mouth.

item.title: Molecular residual disease interception in locoregionally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: The MERIDIAN Phase II trial.

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Molecular residual disease (MRD) interception has not been studied in locoregionally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC). MERIDIAN evaluates whether rilvegostomig, an anti-PD-1/TIGIT bispecific antibody, could clear ctDNA in MRD setting. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with stage III HPV-positive or stage III-IVB HPV-negative LA-HNSCC received definitive treatment (surgery ± adjuvant therapy, radiation, or chemoradiation). ctDNA was assessed using an exome-based tumor-informed assay at baseline and surveillance. Patients with detectable ctDNA during MRD window (8-12 weeks post-definitive therapy), no progression, and PD-L1 ≥1 were eligible for randomization (3:1) to rilvegostomig or observation. Plasma HPV DNA was evaluated using HPV sequencing. RESULTS: Of 52 enrolled patients, 42 were evaluable; 57% had oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), mostly treated with chemoradiation. Six patients (14%) were ctDNA positive at the MRD window: 3 had progression, 1 had PD-L1 <1, 1 received rilvegostomig, and 1 was observed. The treated MRD-positive patient achieved ctDNA clearance at 10 weeks and remained recurrence-free through 23.4 months of follow-up. The two untreated MRD-positive patients showed substantial lead times to progression (190 and 235 days). Excluding the treated patient, ctDNA positivity at the MRD window was associated with worse RFS (HR 16.9; 95% CI 4.4-64.7) and OS (HR 5.3; 95% CI 1.2-22.2). In HPV-positive OPC, plasma HPV DNA correlated with worse RFS (p=0.02). Combined ctDNA and HPV DNA achieved 100% sensitivity and 73% specificity. CONCLUSIONS: ctDNA detection post-treatment predicts outcomes in LA-HNSCC. MERIDIAN provides preliminary evidence for MRD interception with rilvegostomig, showing durable ctDNA clearance.

item.title: Association between duodenal mucosa-associated periodontal bacteria and advanced liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
item.dc:creator: Niida K, Yamamoto Y, Miyake T, Hayashi M, Tange K, Watanabe T, Yoshida O, Tokumoto Y, Tomida H, Takeshita E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Niida K, Yamamoto Y, Miyake T, Hayashi M, Tange K, Watanabe T, Yoshida O, Tokumoto Y, Tomida H, Takeshita E, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0363551

Abstract:
Gut microbiota and periodontal diseases are potential risk factors for duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota in fibrosis progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease; however, the specific contribution of duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota remains unclear. Therefore, in this prospective study, we investigated its association with liver stiffness to elucidate its role in disease progression. Duodenal brush samples were collected during endoscopy from patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, classified by liver stiffness measurement into advanced (liver stiffness measurement>8.7 kPa, n = 10) and non-advanced (n = 20) groups. Extracted DNA was subjected to shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Analyses included taxonomy, diversity, differential abundance (edgeR), correlation (Spearman), and receiver operating characteristic predictive modeling, focusing on periodontal bacteria. While microbial diversity did not differ, advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease was characterized by the enrichment of the phylum Pseudomonadota and the genera Haemophilus and Klebsiella. Eight periodontal bacteria, including Campylobacter rectus, Porphyromonas gingivalis, and Fusobacterium nucleatum, were significantly enriched in patients with advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (P < 0.05) and correlated with liver fibrosis markers. A model based on these bacteria discriminated advanced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI, 0.634-1.000). Duodenal mucosa-associated microbiota alterations, particularly the enrichment of eight periodontal species, were associated with fibrosis severity. These findings highlight the role of the oral-gut-liver axis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease progression and suggest potential microbial biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

item.title: In vitro functional evaluation of toothbrushes using two standardized models of the smooth and interproximal surface model.
item.dc:creator: Endoh M, Tsuji Y, Jinushi T, Kurihara S, Higuchi T, Takayanagi A, Yamagishi A, Nomoto T
item.description:
Authors: Endoh M, Tsuji Y, Jinushi T, Kurihara S, Higuchi T, Takayanagi A, Yamagishi A, Nomoto T
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0338683
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43077421



Abstract:
Manual toothbrushes are the most widely used for daily plaque control.　Although proper toothbrushing technique is crucial for effective plaque removal, improving and sustaining these skills remains challenging. Consequently, selecting an appropriate toothbrush is essential for maintaining optimal oral health. Despite various toothbrushes available, objective evaluation of the functional index of a toothbrush remains elusive. This study aimed to develop a comprehensive and objective evaluation method for toothbrush function using standardized models. For comprehensive evaluation, the assessed surface was divided into three elements (convex, concave, and flat). Two standardized evaluation models were developed: the smooth and interproximal surface model, which assesses the cleaning ability of both smooth and interproximal surfaces, and the single half cylinder model (SHC model), which measures the following ability of the toothbrush bristles on convex surfaces. Two types of test toothbrushes were used: small toothbrush with simple structure (toothbrush S) and large, functionally designed toothbrush (toothbrush G). Statistical analyses were performed using t‑tests and Bonferroni correction was applied when multiple comparisons were performed. The results indicated that toothbrush G had equal or greater cleaning ability than toothbrush S across all tested angles in the smooth and interproximal surface model. The minimum following load necessary for effective cleaning without bristle bounce was significantly lower (p = 0.01) for toothbrush G (1.25 N) than for toothbrush S (3.84 N), suggesting that toothbrush G is less dependent on brushing technique and more suitable for a wide range of individuals, regardless of their brushing skills. In this study, we confirmed that it is possible to significantly detect differences in toothbrush functionality (cleaning and following ability of toothbrush) by using two in vitro models of partial tooth-surface. Continued development of these models can potentially contribute to the standardization of toothbrush evaluation.

item.title: Geographic and Socioeconomic Disparities in Stage at Diagnosis and Nodal Burden Among Patients With HPV-Era Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma in Louisiana: A Population-Based Analysis.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stage at diagnosis is a strong predictor of survival in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). Gulf South population-level data on these disparities remain limited. METHODS: We analyzed 1344 patients with known stage at diagnosis from Louisiana Tumor Registry data (n = 1698 cases, 2018-2023). Geographic access was operationalized as straight-line distance from parish centroid to the nearest academic medical center (AMC), categorized as < 25, 25-50, and > 50 miles. item.title: Blinded Evaluation of Patient-Facing Thyroid Cancer Information From Clinicians, Large Language Models, and Web Search.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Nov-24

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the quality of patient-facing thyroid cancer information generated by clinicians, large language models (LLMs), and web search results using parallel expert and layperson evaluation under blinded conditions. STUDY DESIGN: Blinded comparative evaluation study. SETTING: Online, text-based assessment of patient-facing health information. METHODS: Thirty commonly searched thyroid cancer questions were identified using Google Trends. For each question, patient-facing answers were generated by a fellowship-trained head and neck surgeon, 5 widely used LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek), and the first nonsponsored Google search result. Responses were anonymised and source-blinded. Seven attending physicians evaluated responses using the Quality Analysis of Medical AI (QAMAI) framework across 5 domains, and 15 lay participants evaluated the same responses across 4 patient-centred domains. Ratings were analysed at the question level using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Friedman tests, Kendall's W, and post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: Expert inter-rater reliability was good across domains (ICC 0.78-0.82). Expert ratings differed significantly across sources (P < .001; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.81), with Claude achieving the highest expert scores and Google-derived responses the lowest. Layperson ratings also differed significantly (P < .001; Kendall's W = 0.70-0.87) but clustered near the upper end of the scale, indicating a ceiling effect. The largest expert-rated differences occurred for treatment-related questions, particularly radioactive iodine therapy. CONCLUSION: Patient-facing thyroid cancer information quality varies across clinicians, LLMs, and web search results. Divergence between expert and layperson assessments indicates that perceived clarity and reassurance do not reliably reflect expert-defined completeness or clinical robustness.

Abstract:
Nasal septal perforation (NSP) is a known complication of nasal trauma such as surgery or cauterization, intranasal drug use, autoinflammatory or autoimmune conditions, and infection. Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis (CV) is a less common cause of NSP in which immune complexes precipitate in and occlude small vessels, leading to ischemic necrosis of the nasal septal mucosa. This is a case report of a 75-year-old female patient with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and associated type I CV who presented with longstanding, recurrent bilateral nasal crusting, and was found to have a large anterior NSP with normal-appearing margins. Given her otherwise unremarkable medical or social history, her presentation was most likely attributable to the known CV. Biopsy to rule out malignancy was deferred, and it was anticipated that there would significant improvement in sinonasal symptoms with treatment of the underlying conditions. Therefore, the patient was initiated on low dose prednisone with subsequent taper, in addition to pre-existing plasma cell-directed therapy and dexamethasone, and the nasal crusting and drainage significantly improved after 2 weeks without need for surgical intervention.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumocephalus typically results from craniofacial trauma, tumors, infections, or skull base defects. Acute pneumocephalus in a patient without prior neurological history or obvious skull base defects presents a diagnostic challenge. CASE PRESENTATION: A 65-year-old male with a history of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and multiple esophageal dilations post-radiation presented with hypercapnic respiratory failure. He developed acute-onset altered mental status after initiation of Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure (BiPAP). An urgent head computed tomography (CT) scan showed pneumocephalus, and subsequent sinus CTs showed no skull base defects. Nasal endoscopy showed no obvious clear fluid drainage, and nasal secretions tested negative for beta-2 transferrin. Retrospective review of a chest CT from 3 months prior revealed a small proximal esophageal defect with prevertebral air tracking. Follow-up CT imaging confirmed air tracking along the T1 costovertebral joint, identifying an enterothecal fistula as the route for positive-pressure air entry into the spinal canal and cranial vault. The pneumocephalus resolved within 10 days with conservative measures. Although surgical obliteration of the fistula was discussed, the patient opted against surgical intervention. CONCLUSION: Spontaneous or positive-pressure-induced pneumocephalus without a skull base defect should prompt investigation of alternative air-entry pathways, including enterothecal fistulas, particularly in patients with predisposing risk factors such as esophageal malignancy and dilations.

item.title: Sustaining rural cultural memory through oral history: A case study of spatial reconstruction in a demolished village.
item.dc:creator: Zhang T, Ding C, Cheng X, Yang C, Zheng D, Chen K
item.description:
Authors: Zhang T, Ding C, Cheng X, Yang C, Zheng D, Chen K
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0362355
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43071660



Abstract:
Rapid urbanization and large-scale village demolition in China have erased many traditional rural settlements from the physical landscape, but not from residents' memories. How to reconstruct these invisible spaces and sustain local culture in the absence of material fabric remains an underexplored question in rural sustainability research. This qualitative case study focuses on Shixinzhuang, a demolished village now occupied by the new campus of Zhengzhou University in central China. We conducted in-depth oral history interviews with six long-term residents selected through purposive sampling based on native attachment, spatial role, and generational span. During interviews, participants drew cognitive maps starting from their own courtyards to locate streets, public facilities, production zones, and ritual spaces. Hand-drawn maps were systematically organized and compared to identify shared spatial patterns and memory discrepancies. This information was further cross-verified through data triangulation with archival photographs, satellite imagery, field revisits, and focused validation discussions. Data analysis centered on themes of spatial memory, memory places, and cultural sustainability. Findings indicate that despite the complete demolition of the physical village, Shixinzhuang's spatial structure can still be systematically reconstructed from villagers' memories. Residents consistently recalled the village's evolution from a walled enclosure to an open, expanding settlement. Its spatial organization was structured around a "cross-street" skeleton formed by a north-south main street and an east-west auxiliary street, with housing in the central area growing organically while peripheral housing was more orderly. Spatial memories were highly clustered around several "memory places," notably the Nainai Miao (Grandmother Temple), ancestral grave areas, and residential rooftop platforms. Even after relocation, these places continue to carry kinship ties, religious rituals, and neighborhood interactions. Furthermore, production spaces reflected layered institutional experiences transitioning from collective agriculture to a marginal industrial belt, with distinct intergenerational differences emerging in narratives differentiating between "collective labor" and "earning money in the brick kilns." Ultimately, the joint process of narration, mapping, and iterative correction transformed the oral history practice from a unidirectional recording into a reflexive, participatory act of "re-creating place." This study demonstrates that even when a traditional village has disappeared from the ground, its spatial structure and symbolic places can be recovered through the combined use of oral history and cognitive mapping, and mobilized as resources for rural cultural sustainability. For demolished settlements, integrating narrative-based spatial reconstruction into planning, heritage management, and community-building can help re-anchor local identity, inform commemorative and interpretive design, and institutionalize residents' narrative participation in rural spatial governance.

item.title: Multitarget docking and toxicity-guided prioritisation of phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against wheat fungal pathogens.
item.dc:creator: Ope MS, Ashrafuzzaman M
item.description:
Authors: Ope MS, Ashrafuzzaman M
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0356864
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43071659



Abstract:
The rising issue of fungicide resistance, along with environmental concerns related to synthetic fungicides, highlights the need for safer and more sustainable antifungal agents. In this computational study, we screened nineteen phytochemicals from locally available medicinal plants in Bangladesh against three fungal protein targets associated with major wheat diseases: class I sesquiterpene synthase (PDB ID: 8H4P) and trichothecene 3-O-acetyltransferase (TRI101; PDB ID: 3B2S) from Fusarium graminearum, and the AvrSr50 effector protein (PDB ID: 7MQQ) from Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici. Blind docking was performed using AutoDock Vina (with an exhaustiveness setting of 16) and evaluated for reliability through consensus docking with CB-Dock2. We analyzed protein-ligand interactions using BIOVIA Discovery Studio, and the top-ranked compounds were further assessed for toxicity and ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) properties with ProTox-3 and ADMETlab 3.0. Thevetin B, Thevetin A, and Uscharin were computationally prioritized as candidate multitarget binders. Notably, Thevetin B formed extensive hydrogen-bond and hydrophobic interaction networks across all three proteins and showed comparatively strong predicted binding affinities. However, ProTox-3 predicted high acute oral toxicity for Thevetin B (LD₅₀ = 4 mg/kg, Class I) and Thevetin A (LD₅₀ = 8 mg/kg, Class II), while Uscharin had a substantially higher predicted LD₅₀ (2000 mg/kg, Class IV). The ADMET analysis revealed shared liabilities such as mutagenicity and nephrotoxicity, along with limited absorption, but also highlighted compound-specific differences in physicochemical properties and environmental toxicity. These findings indicate an efficacy-safety trade-off among the computationally prioritized candidates and support their further evaluation as testable hypotheses rather than establishing a definitive efficacy-safety hierarchy. This study provides a structured computational prioritization of locally available phytochemicals and emphasizes that any claims of practical antifungal utility must be supported by experimental validation of both efficacy and safety.

item.title: Comparison of the 2015 and 2025 American Thyroid Association Risk Stratification Systems in Predicting Recurrence in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Kim NH, Kim CA, Lee YM, Sung TY, Song DE, Kim TY, Kim WG, Jeon MJ
item.description:
Authors: Kim NH, Kim CA, Lee YM, Sung TY, Song DE, Kim TY, Kim WG, Jeon MJ
Journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association | DOI: 10.1177/10507256261510177
Published: 2026-Nov-23

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk stratification systems are essential for individualized management of differentiated thyroid cancer. This study compared the 2015 and 2025 American Thyroid Association (ATA) guidelines in predicting long-term recurrence risk in patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 2677 adult patients with PTC who underwent total thyroidectomy at a tertiary academic center between 2010 and 2015. Patients were stratified according to the 2015 and 2025 ATA guidelines. The primary outcome was structural persistent or recurrent disease (clinical event). RESULTS: Risk distribution differed significantly between the two systems, with 526 patients (19.6%) upstaged under the 2025 ATA guidelines. Compared with the 2015 ATA system, the 2025 ATA system assigned fewer patients to the low-risk group (27.8% vs. 15.1%) and more to the high-risk group (9.9% vs. 16.8%). By the 2015 ATA, 1668 patients (62.3%) were classified as intermediate-risk. By the 2025 ATA, 882 (32.9%) and 940 patients (35.1%) were classified as low-intermediate- and intermediate-high-risk, respectively. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years (interquartile range: 6.6-12.2 years), 132 (4.9%) patients experienced clinical events. Event rates among low-risk patients were 1.2% under the 2015 ATA system and 0.7% under the 2025 ATA system. Among intermediate-risk patients, the event rate was 4.4% with the 2015 ATA guidelines, compared with 0.9% and 5.3% in the low-intermediate and intermediate-high groups, respectively, under the 2025 ATA system. Among high-risk patients, event rates were 18.5% and 15.7% under the 2015 and 2025 ATA systems, respectively. Harrell's C-index was 0.711 ([confidence interval or CI, 0.672-0.750]) for the 2015 ATA classification and 0.781 ([CI, 0.748-0.814]) for the 2025 ATA classification, with a difference of 0.069 ([CI, 0.042-0.097]; p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 ATA risk stratification system was more granular, showed improved discrimination, and more precisely identified patients at very low risk of recurrence. However, a substantial proportion of patients were reclassified into higher-risk categories, which may have implications for potential overtreatment and warrants careful consideration.

item.title: Long-Term Nonmalignant Chronic Health Conditions in Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma Survivors and the Impact of Radioactive Iodine Therapy: Evidence from Real-World Data.
item.dc:creator: Yackobovitch-Gavan M, Bello R, Oron T, Lazar L, Hayek S
item.description:
Authors: Yackobovitch-Gavan M, Bello R, Oron T, Lazar L, Hayek S
Journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association | DOI: 10.1177/10507256261505406
Published: 2026-Nov-23
PMID: 43071370



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) is the most common endocrine malignancy in children, adolescents, and young adults (CAYA) with survival exceeding 98%. Real-world data on long-term nonmalignant chronic health conditions (CHCs) remain scarce. OBJECTIVE: To characterize long-term nonmalignant CHCs in CAYA DTC survivors relative to cancer-free controls and explore associations with radioactive iodine (RAI) exposure. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Clalit Health Services electronic health records (Israel, 1982-2022) comparing 5267 DTC survivors (diagnosed at age < 40) with 21,062 matched cancer-free controls. Incident CHCs occurring ≥2 years post-DTC diagnosis/index-date were assessed across metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, skeletal, autoimmune/rheumatologic, and emotional domains and were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RAI subgroup analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 14.7 years (interquartile range 8.8-23.2), the risk of developing ≥1 CHC did not differ significantly between DTC survivors and cancer-free controls (54.4% vs. 52.0%; HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.11; p = 0.066). Survivors were more likely to experience multimorbidity (≥2 CHCs 35.7% vs. 32.0%) and had higher risks of several specific organ-system conditions: osteoporosis (HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.14-1.56), chronic kidney disease (HR 1.61; 95% CI: 1.32-1.96), gastroesophageal disorders (HR 1.35; 95% CI: 1.26-1.45), dyslipidemia (HR 1.23; 95% CI: 1.16-1.32), and hypertension (HR 1.21; 95% CI: 1.13-1.29). Pulmonary, cardiovascular, autoimmune, hepatic, and clinically diagnosed emotional disorders did not differ significantly between groups. Exploratory analyses revealed a dose-dependent RAI risk gradient (1 course: HR 1.20; 95% CI: 1.06-1.35; ≥2 courses: HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.16-1.52). CONCLUSIONS: Despite excellent overall survival, CAYA DTC survivors face a modest overall increase in CHC risk alongside notably greater multisystem morbidity. RAI-associated risk trends are exploratory and need further research. These findings support risk-adapted therapy and structured long-term survivorship monitoring.

Published: 2026-Nov-22

Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Free flap reconstruction has become the gold standard after major oncologic resections in the head and neck (HN) region. Despite advances in techniques, free flaps undergo volumetric and structural changes over time, potentially compromising functional and aesthetic outcomes. This study aims to explore a solid three-dimensional method to perform multiparametric assessment of free flaps. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A cohort of 32 patients undergoing ablative HN surgery followed by free flap reconstruction was studied, using postoperative CT/MRI scans at fixed intervals. Semi-automatic 3D segmentation was adopted to measure soft tissue flap parameters, excluding bone. Both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses examined dimensional changes, separating fasciocutaneous and muscular components. RESULTS: Cross-sectional analysis showed significant dimensional variability among anatomical subsites, particularly in the volume and thickness of fasciocutaneous components. Longitudinal data revealed that muscular flap components underwent significantly greater reductions in diameter, surface area, and volume compared to fasciocutaneous tissue, which remained relatively stable over time. No significant differences in dimensional changes were observed between different flap types overtime. CONCLUSION: This study presents a reproducible 3D methodology for multiparametric assessment of free flaps in HN reconstruction. The marked reduction in muscular components relative to fasciocutaneous tissues highlights the importance of considering differential shrinkage in surgical planning and potential overcorrection. Future prospective studies with larger cohorts and earlier imaging are needed to validate and optimize reconstructive strategies.

item.title: CBCT-based radiomics of the crista galli: association with an exploratory composite anatomical complexity framework in a preliminary study.
item.dc:creator: Uzun S, Cakan KN, Magat G
item.description:
Authors: Uzun S, Cakan KN, Magat G
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10833-5
Published: 2026-Nov-22
PMID: 43069002



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between CBCT-based radiomic features of the crista galli (CG) and anterior skull base anatomical complexity using the exploratory Anatomical Complexity Score (ACS). METHODS: This retrospective exploratory pilot study included 50 CBCT images. CG anatomy was evaluated using the Keros, Komut-Golpinar, Hajiioannou, and pneumatization classifications and integrated into the exploratory ACS framework. Following three-dimensional segmentation, 107 radiomic features were extracted. Associations between radiomic features and ACS were analyzed, and exploratory linear and logistic regression models were developed. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: Thirty participants (60.0%) were classified as low complexity and 20 (40.0%) as moderate complexity; no high-complexity cases were identified. Among the four constituent classifications, Keros showed the largest internal association with the composite ACS (p < 0.001, ε² = 0.372). Several radiomic features showed nominal correlations with continuous ACS and unadjusted differences between ACS-based groups. None of the correlations with continuous ACS remained statistically significant after FDR correction; subsequent ROC and modeling analyses were treated as exploratory. In exploratory ROC analyses based on features identified in the unadjusted analyses, GLSZM Size Zone Non-Uniformity demonstrated the highest moderate discriminative performance for differentiating low- and moderate-complexity groups (AUC = 0.743), followed by GLDM Dependence Non-Uniformity (AUC = 0.733) and GLCM Cluster Prominence (AUC = 0.718). The exploratory radiomics-only logistic regression model demonstrated an apparent AUC of 0.743, while 5-fold cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.715. CONCLUSIONS: CBCT-based radiomic features of the CG showed exploratory associations with ACS. However, none of the correlations with continuous ACS remained statistically significant after FDR correction. The proposed ACS framework should therefore be regarded as a preliminary exploratory tool rather than a validated clinical outcome-prediction tool. Further validation in larger independent cohorts is required before any clinical application.

item.title: Surgical margins in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: A European Head and Neck Society (EHNS) multidisciplinary modified Delphi consensus.
item.dc:creator: Pamuk E, Ferrari M, Kraak JT, Singer S, Taylor KJ, Dietz A, Mäkitie AA, von Buchwald C, Kyrodimos E, Crosetti E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Pamuk E, Ferrari M, Kraak JT, Singer S, Taylor KJ, Dietz A, Mäkitie AA, von Buchwald C, Kyrodimos E, Crosetti E, et al.
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108243
Published: 2026-Nov-22
PMID: 43068514



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical margin assessment in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) remains poorly standardized by HPV status, subsite, and treatment context. This European Head and Neck Society (EHNS) consensus aimed to harmonize margin assessment and margin-based decisions. METHODS: Following systematic review, 25 multidisciplinary panelists evaluated recommendations through two Delphi rounds; consensus was ≥80 % and near-consensus 70-79.9 %. Margindefinitionswerebasedonformalin-fixed,paraffin-embeddedsections,notintraoperativeor postoperativegrossingestimates. RESULTS: Of 48 recommendations, 32 reached consensus, six near-consensus, and 10 were rejected. "Ink on tumor" defined a positive margin irrespective of HPV status (96 %). A 5-mm mucosal margin was retained for HPV-negative OPSCC (84 %), whereas 3 mm reached near-consensus for HPV-positive disease (78.3 %); smaller thresholds were unsupported. A clear margin alone should not determine adjuvant treatment (78.3 %, near-consensus). Re-resection was recommended when the margin site was identifiable and would change adjuvant management. Positive margins warranted radiotherapy in pT1-T2 HPV-positive disease without other adverse features (80 %), whereas chemoradiotherapy was recommended with high-risk features, such as pT3-T4 disease or extranodal extension (95.8 %), and in HPV-negative disease (100 %). For close margins, selective de-escalation could be considered in highly selected HPV-positive disease without high-risk features (82.6 %), whereas HPV-negative disease warranted radiotherapy, with escalation according to additional risks (91.3 %). In fit patients aged ≥70 years with positive margins, radiotherapy alone was favored for HPV-positive disease (87.5 %), while chemoradiotherapy was retained for fit patients with HPV-negative disease (95.7 %). CONCLUSIONS: This consensus provides a multidisciplinary framework for harmonized OPSCC margin assessment and risk-adapted postoperative management across HPV status, anatomy, and treatment-related morbidity.

item.title: Human Papillomavirus Knowledge and Vaccine Receptiveness of County Hospital Otolaryngology Patients.
item.dc:creator: Chen S, Evans LK, Lin ME, Sayeed S, St John MA, Han PS, Chhetri DK
item.description:
Authors: Chen S, Evans LK, Lin ME, Sayeed S, St John MA, Han PS, Chhetri DK
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71021
Published: 2026-Nov-22
PMID: 43068467



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates human papillomavirus (HPV) knowledge and vaccine receptiveness among patients at an otolaryngology clinic in a county hospital setting. METHODS: Surveys were provided to adult patients between September 2023 and July 2026. Surveys were offered in English and Spanish and assessed awareness of HPV, knowledge of association with cervical and oropharyngeal cancers, and willingness to undergo HPV vaccination. Demographic data including sex, age, race/ethnicity, vaccination status, and HPV-related disease were also collected. Chi-squared and Fisher's exact test compared differences between males and females. RESULTS: Two hundred and one patients completed the questionnaire with demographic data available in 86. Most were Spanish-speaking, female, Hispanic, and not vaccinated against HPV. 52.2% (105/201) had heard of HPV while 25.1% (50/199) knew HPV could cause oropharyngeal cancer. Almost three-fifths had not heard of the HPV vaccine (60.2%, 121/201), but if offered, 33.0% (64/194) were open to receiving it. Compared with males, females were statistically more likely to have heard of HPV, understand its association with cervical and oropharyngeal cancer, and believe in the HPV vaccine's efficacy. There were no statistical differences by sex in willingness to receive the vaccine, if offered. CONCLUSION: There is low HPV health literacy and vaccination rates among this county otolaryngology clinic population. Despite this, these patients are highly receptive to receiving the vaccine if offered. Patient education and point-of-care HPV vaccination at otolaryngology visits represent a highly feasible, scalable intervention to bypass primary care barriers and reduce HPV-related disease. item.title: Allogeneic umbilical cord-mesenchymal stem/stromal cells for chronic radiation-induced xerostomia: a phase I study with multimodal functional and imaging assessment.
item.dc:creator: Švajger U, Mitrovič G, Hartman K, Ležaić L, Kokalj M, Plavc G, Prešeren U, Blatnik O, Bavec A, Sočan A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Švajger U, Mitrovič G, Hartman K, Ležaić L, Kokalj M, Plavc G, Prešeren U, Blatnik O, Bavec A, Sočan A, et al.
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.10.058
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43067442



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Radiation-induced xerostomia is a clinically significant adverse effect of head and neck radiotherapy with limited treatment options. This prospective, single-arm case series evaluated the safety, feasibility, and exploratory clinical efficacy of ultrasound-guided intraglandular administration of allogeneic umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (UC-MSCs) in patients with chronic radiation-induced xerostomia. METHODS AND MATERIALS: Ten disease-free survivors of oropharyngeal cancer with CTCAE grade 2-3 xerostomia received ultrasound-guided UC-MSC injections into both parotid and submandibular glands. Each parotid gland received 50 × 10⁶ UC-MSCs and each submandibular gland 25 × 10⁶ UC-MSCs. Safety was the primary outcome. Exploratory assessments were performed at baseline and at 1 and 4 months and included patient-reported outcome measures, unstimulated and stimulated salivary flow rates, salivary biochemical analyses, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound shear-wave elastography, salivary gland scintigraphy, and, where feasible, core-needle biopsy. RESULTS: No serious adverse events were observed. Procedure-related effects were limited to transient injection-site pain, swelling, and local discomfort. Objective salivary flow rates and most biochemical parameters remained stable throughout follow-up. In contrast, patient-reported outcomes improved, with the greatest changes at 4 months. Xerostomia Questionnaire scores decreased from 63.44 ± 16.81 at baseline to 53.18 ± 21.16 at 4 months (p = 0.0066), and visual analogue scale scores from 64.65 ± 17.30 to 60.29 ± 18.11 (p = 0.0122). Improvements were also observed in xerostomia and sticky saliva domains of the EORTC QLQ-H&N35. MRI showed only subtle changes in T2-weighted signal intensity ratios, while elastography remained unchanged. Scintigraphy demonstrated increased excretion velocity at 4 months (p = 0.0355). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-arm case series of 10 patients, ultrasound-guided intraglandular UC-MSC administration was feasible and well tolerated over four months, with no serious adverse events. Improvements in PROMs and scintigraphic excretion velocity were exploratory findings in the absence of a control group and occurred despite largely unchanged salivary flow. Clinical efficacy remains to be established in adequately powered, randomized, placebo-controlled trials.

item.title: Characterization of the peri-tumoral immune infiltrate at the invasive front of oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma.

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our objectives were to determine the association between high peri-tumoral immune infiltrate (PTII) and survival, determine the association between cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and PTII and to characterize immune cell density at the invasive front of oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 303 patients with OCSCC were categorized into low and high PTII on whole block sections using histopathological grading. item.title: Association between statin use and postoperative recurrence in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis: a single-center retrospective observational study.

Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10818-4
Published: 2026-Nov-21
PMID: 43066758



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS), a type 2-dominant form of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, is characterized by frequent postoperative relapse. Although statins exhibit pleiotropic anti-inflammatory and profibrinolytic properties that may mitigate impaired fibrinolysis in ECRS, their clinical impact remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between statin use and postoperative recurrence in patients with ECRS undergoing functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS). METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, observational study included patients diagnosed with ECRS according to the Japanese Epidemiological Survey of Refractory Eosinophilic Chronic Rhinosinusitis criteria who underwent FESS between April 2015 and December 2025. Postoperative recurrence was defined as the need for any of the following treatment escalations: revision surgery, systemic oral corticosteroid therapy, local triamcinolone administration, or use of (or eligibility for) biologic therapy. RESULTS: Forty-nine patients completed at least 6 months of follow-up, including 11 statin users (22.4%). Statin users were significantly older than non-users (60.9 vs. 52.3 years; p=0.033), whereas other baseline characteristics were comparable. Statin use was associated with lower odds of overall postoperative recurrence (27.3% vs. 63.2%; OR 0.22; 95% CI 0.05-0.96; p=0.046). In exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for age and asthma, the association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.06-1.32; p=0.115). CONCLUSION: Statin use was associated with lower odds of overall postoperative recurrence in patients with ECRS. However, this association was attenuated after adjustment for age and asthma and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

item.title: Pretreatment total gross tumor volume complements TNM staging in predicting survival in locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.

item.description:
Authors: Delikaya M, Özkaya Akagündüz Ö, Hazeral YZ, Esassolak M

Abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the prognostic significance of pretreatment gross tumor volume (GTV) and determine whether volumetric assessment provides additional prognostic value beyond conventional TNM staging in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy. METHODS: This retrospective study included 124 patients treated with definitive radiotherapy between 2012 and 2024; 117 received concurrent systemic therapy. Pretreatment GTVprimary, GTVnodal, and GTVtotal were measured on planning CT for patients treated with upfront radiotherapy and on the CT component of pre-induction PET/CT for patients receiving induction chemotherapy. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to determine cutoff values. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. The incremental prognostic value of volumetric parameters was assessed using Akaike's Information Criterion (AIC)-based model comparison. RESULTS: The selected cutoff value for GTVtotal was 36 cc. Although GTVprimary showed the highest AUC in ROC analysis, GTVtotal remained associated with disease-specific survival after multivariable adjustment and yielded the lowest AIC among the compared models. Patients with GTVtotal > 36 cc had poorer disease-specific survival. GTVtotal, T stage, and age > 60 years were independently associated with disease-specific survival. CONCLUSION: Pretreatment GTVtotal provides complementary prognostic information beyond conventional TNM staging and may improve risk stratification in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy. The data-derived cutoff requires external validation before clinical use. The 36-cc threshold may be influenced by the predominance of hypopharyngeal tumors in the high-volume group and should be applied cautiously to laryngeal cancer cohorts.

item.title: Sentinel lymph node biopsy using ICG-[99mTc]Tc-nanocolloid and superselective level I dissection.
item.dc:creator: Heldens GTN, Weijs WLJ, Arens AIJ, van Rijk MC, Janssen MJR, van Engen-van Grunsven I, Honings J, Coppen C, Verhoeven T, Takes RP
item.description:
