CONCLUSIONS: This is the largest single center analysis of DM OPSCC to date. Primary DM OPSCC was associated with worse survival and lower HPV-positivity. Patients with DM, particularly those with HPV-positive disease, may achieve extended survival following aggressive treatment such as MDT.

item.title: TNM Staging in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Evolution, Validation, and Priorities for Refinement.
item.dc:creator: Shan KC, Zhou R, Niu CQ, Shi WT, He Y, Zhang ZY
item.description:
Authors: Shan KC, Zhou R, Niu CQ, Shi WT, He Y, Zhang ZY
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223674
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43088203



Abstract:
Tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) staging standardizes the description of disease extent in oral squamous cell carcinoma. The eighth edition of the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging system incorporated depth of invasion into T classification and extranodal extension into N classification. This narrative review examines the evidence underlying these revisions, their validation, and priorities for further refinement. Multicenter cohorts, registry analyses, and systematic reviews generally support improved prognostic stratification, although gains in discrimination vary and are often modest. Measurement variability and heterogeneous outcomes within categories remain important limitations. We propose an evaluation roadmap that links each candidate to a defined classification weakness, reproducible measurement, independent incremental value, and feasibility. For patients treated with upfront surgery, positive-node count combined with extranodal extension status warrants first priority for evaluation, followed by standardized bone-invasion descriptors. Quantitative extranodal extension requires further standardization. Additional pathological features and prediction models may complement individualized risk assessment. Current evidence neither establishes a ceiling for anatomical staging nor demonstrates that further anatomical subdivision alone will resolve residual risk variation. Retaining TNM as the core staging system and supplementing it with validated models is a practical approach. Hybrid stage groupings require separate evaluation. Clinical, pathological, and post-treatment settings should remain distinct. These priorities reflect evidence synthesis and author interpretation, not guideline-level recommendations. Greater prognostic accuracy alone does not establish treatment benefit.

item.title: Impact of positional obstructive sleep apnea phenotype on mandibular advancement therapy outcomes: A multicenter cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Nicoletti S, De Virgilio A, Terranova S, Brunori M, Vicini C, Campisi R, De Ceglie V, Casale M, Moffa A, Maniaci A, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Nicoletti S, De Virgilio A, Terranova S, Brunori M, Vicini C, Campisi R, De Ceglie V, Casale M, Moffa A, Maniaci A, et al.
Journal: American journal of otolaryngology | DOI: 10.1016/j.amjoto.2026.105000
Published: 2026-Nov-17
PMID: 43056883



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Mandibular advancement devices (MADs) are an established treatment for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but reliable predictors of response remain limited. Positional OSA (POSA) has been proposed as a favorable phenotype. This study evaluated whether positional phenotype influences respiratory outcomes and treatment success in patients treated with MAD. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 82 consecutive patients with OSA treated with MAD across six tertiary sleep centers. Baseline and follow-up home sleep apnea tests performed at least 6 months after completion of MAD titration were analyzed. POSA was defined according to Cartwright's criteria as a supine apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) at least twice the non-supine AHI. Outcomes included changes in respiratory parameters and treatment success according to Sher's criteria (≥50% AHI reduction and post-treatment AHI <20 events/h). RESULTS: Fifty patients had POSA and 32 had non-POSA. MAD therapy significantly improved total AHI, oxygen desaturation index, and oxygenation parameters in both groups. Treatment success occurred in 42/50 POSA patients (84.0%) and 30/32 non-POSA patients (93.8%; p = 0.332). Reductions in total AHI were also comparable between groups (19.19 ± 15.50 vs 24.14 ± 19.60 events/h; p = 0.232). Likewise, rates of achieving AHI <10 and <5 events/h did not differ significantly between groups. Positional phenotype was not significantly associated with treatment success. CONCLUSIONS: MAD therapy was associated with respiratory improvement regardless of positional phenotype. These findings do not support using POSA alone as a criterion for selecting candidates for MAD therapy. Larger prospective studies are required to confirm these results.

item.title: Gas Plasma Exposure Triggers Specific Metabolite and Drug-Resistance-Related Membrane Transporter Gene Expression Across 12 Cancer Cell Lines.
item.dc:creator: Singer D, Knierim J, McKeever L, Berner J, Miebach L, Huebner L, Schmidt A, Bekeschus S
item.description:
Authors: Singer D, Knierim J, McKeever L, Berner J, Miebach L, Huebner L, Schmidt A, Bekeschus S
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223662
Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43088191



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Plasma medicine has emerged as a promising approach for cancer treatment, with reactive oxygen and nitrogen species generated by plasma contributing to cellular stress and tumor cell death. However, the effects of plasma treatment on membrane transporter regulation remain poorly understood. METHODS: This study investigated whether plasma exposure alters the gene expression of pharmacologically and biologically relevant transporters across diverse cancer cell lines, and whether these responses are conserved in an in ovo tumor model. Twelve cancer cell lines representing squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma, and adenocarcinoma were treated with plasma at cell line-specific IC25 conditions. The expression of ten transporter genes was assessed by targeted quantitative PCR. RESULTS: Plasma treatment induced heterogeneous changes in transporter gene expression, with both up- and downregulation observed across cell lines and transporters. SLC2A2, ABCC2, SLCO3A1, and SLC28A3 displayed particularly pronounced and distinct response patterns. Correlation analysis further identified coordinated changes among several transporter genes, suggesting shared response patterns to plasma-induced stress. Selected transporter responses were subsequently assessed in an in ovo tumor model, revealing partial conservation of plasma-induced transcriptional regulation alongside substantial context-dependent differences in response magnitude and direction. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that plasma treatment can modulate transporter gene expression in a heterogeneous and cell line-dependent manner. The observed regulation may reflect broader cellular adaptations to plasma-induced stress and could have implications for cellular drug handling and pharmacological response.

item.title: Evaluation of the Clinicopathologic and Genomic Features of CNS Metastases in Soft Tissue Sarcoma.
item.dc:creator: Shahnam A, DiConza K, Desir-Camille R, Jee J, Reinhorn D, Babatunde O, Kelly CM, Saoud C, Singer S, Crago AM, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Shahnam A, DiConza K, Desir-Camille R, Jee J, Reinhorn D, Babatunde O, Kelly CM, Saoud C, Singer S, Crago AM, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223659
Published: 2026-Nov-16
PMID: 43088188



Abstract:
Background: The incidence and risk factors for central nervous system (CNS) metastases in soft tissue sarcoma (STS) are poorly defined. We evaluated the frequency of CNS metastases in STS and associated clinicopathologic and genomic factors. Methods: This retrospective study used the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center institutional cBioPortal database. Patients with invasive STS, including gastrointestinal stromal tumor, were included. CNS metastases were identified using natural language processing-derived radiology annotations and confirmed by manual chart review. Cumulative incidence was estimated with death as a competing event. Clinicopathologic and genomic associations were evaluated using Firth logistic regression with correction for multiplicity; post-CNS metastasis survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results: A total of 5379 patients were included. CNS metastases were identified in 161 patients (3.0%), with a 10-year cumulative incidence of 4.5% after accounting for death as a competing event. Median overall survival after CNS metastasis was 4.76 months (95% CI, 3.9-7.5). In one-versus-rest analyses, increased odds of CNS metastasis were observed for alveolar soft part sarcoma (OR 16.61, 95% CI 7.21-35.81; q < 0.001), rhabdomyosarcoma (OR 2.44, 95% CI 1.42-3.97; q = 0.007), non-uterine leiomyosarcoma (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.45-3.34; q = 0.003), extremity primaries (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.58-3.05; q < 0.001), head and neck primaries (OR 2.11, 95% CI 1.26-3.35; q = 0.017), and PDGFRB alterations (OR 4.90, 95% CI 2.29-9.41; q = 0.016). KIT alterations were associated with lower odds (OR 0.10, 95% CI 0.02-0.29; q < 0.001). Conclusions: CNS metastases in STS were uncommon but associated with poor survival, with risk varying by histology and primary site.

item.title: Diagnostic Performance of CT and MRI, Individually and in Combination, in the Assessment of Mandibular Invasion Using Histopathology as a Reference Standard.
item.dc:creator: Rehal S, Kotecha S, Ameerally P, Vaidhyanath R, Menon I, Sahota B, Hashesh H, Lakshmiah R, Mair M
item.description:
Authors: Rehal S, Kotecha S, Ameerally P, Vaidhyanath R, Menon I, Sahota B, Hashesh H, Lakshmiah R, Mair M
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223649
Published: 2026-Nov-14
PMID: 43088179



Abstract:
Background: Mandibular invasion by oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) has important implications for surgical planning. Objective: The objective of the study was to compare the diagnostic performance of computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), individually and in combination, for detecting mandibular invasion in OSCC. The secondary objective was to examine survival according to histopathological invasion status. Methods: Patients with treatment-naïve OSCC who underwent CT and MRI before mandibulectomy between 2016 and 2021 were retrospectively analysed. Imaging findings were compared with histopathology as the reference standard. Combined imaging was considered positive when either CT or MRI demonstrated features of mandibular invasion. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. Results: Among 57 patients, 25 had histopathologically confirmed mandibular invasion. CT and MRI had sensitivities of 88% and 92% and specificities of 90.6% and 87.5%, respectively. Combined imaging had a sensitivity of 96.0% and a specificity of 84.4%. Imaging for cortical invasion had a sensitivity of 88.0% and a specificity of 100%, compared with 92.0% and 87.5% for medullary invasion. Five-year survival was 87.4% in patients without invasion, 55.5% in those with cortical invasion, and 37.8% in those with medullary invasion (log-rank p = 0.015). Conclusions: CT and MRI showed similar overall accuracy. Medullary invasion was associated with poorer survival; however, the survival analysis was univariate and unadjusted.

item.title: Peripheral Granzyme B and Apoptosis-Related Transcriptional Signatures in Laryngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Multiparametric Case-Control Study.
item.dc:creator: Lewandowski F, Wiśniewska K, Pierzynowska K, Grabowski Ł, Zielenkiewicz M, Tychowska A, Radomska K, Niedźwiedzka-Rystwej P
item.description:
Authors: Lewandowski F, Wiśniewska K, Pierzynowska K, Grabowski Ł, Zielenkiewicz M, Tychowska A, Radomska K, Niedźwiedzka-Rystwej P
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223642
Published: 2026-Nov-14
PMID: 43088172



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Peripheral immune-associated changes in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remain incompletely characterised. We investigated selected cytotoxicity- and apoptosis-related transcripts and immune-cell phenotypes in a case-control cohort. METHODS: Peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 35 patients with LSCC and 19 healthy controls were examined using RT-qPCR; circulating CD8+ T and CD16+CD56+ natural killer (NK) populations were assessed by flow cytometry. Granzyme B protein was explored in three available tumour lysates by automated capillary Western blotting. RESULTS: The LSCC group showed higher GZMB and BCL2 transcript abundance and lower BAX and CASP3 abundance (all false-discovery-rate-adjusted q < 0.0001), together with a reduced median BAX/BCL2 transcript ratio (0.107 versus 4.660). Age- and sex-adjusted estimates retained the direction of these associations, although demographic distributions overlapped poorly. The analysed cytometric profiles showed lower proportions of circulating CD8+ T and CD16+CD56+ NK cells and higher fractions expressing intracellular granzyme B. Protein signals were measured descriptively in three tumour lysates. Exploratory multivariate analyses visualised between-group differences. CONCLUSIONS: Marked transcriptional and phenotypic differences were observed between these non-demographically matched groups. The lack of functional assays, limited clinical annotations and substantial age/sex imbalance preclude mechanistic, diagnostic or prognostic conclusions. Independent validation in demographically matched and clinically characterised cohorts is needed.

item.title: Topical Dual PI3K-mTOR Inhibition with Bimiralisib in Actinic Keratosis: From Disease Models to Human Skin Pharmacology.
item.dc:creator: Cmiljanovic V, Cmiljanovic N, Hedberg ML, Mestan J, Yang X, Marshall C, Hebeisen P, Stuetz A, Miller C, Shin T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Cmiljanovic V, Cmiljanovic N, Hedberg ML, Mestan J, Yang X, Marshall C, Hebeisen P, Stuetz A, Miller C, Shin T, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223639
Published: 2026-Nov-13
PMID: 43088168



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Actinic keratosis (AK) is the most common precancerous cutaneous lesion and may progress through squamous cell carcinoma in situ (SCCIS) to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). The PI3K-mTOR pathway is hyperactivated across this spectrum, yet no approved therapy targets it. We evaluated topical bimiralisib (PQR309), a pan-class I PI3K inhibitor with activity against mTOR, and developed a topical bimiralisib gel. Methods: K14-Fyn-Y528F transgenic mice received topical bimiralisib 1% (w/w) or a vehicle daily for 4 weeks, or 50 mg kg-1 orally. Human cSCC explants were incubated with bimiralisib 0.1-10 µmol L-1, and UV-B-irradiated SKH-1 mice received topical bimiralisib 3% (w/w), a vehicle or no treatment, with imiquimod as a comparator. Two of fourteen formulations underwent in vitro release and permeation testing as well as in vivo porcine penetration testing. Results: Topical bimiralisib reduced the lesion area by >99% at 4 weeks, restoring unremarkable epidermis and normalising PI3K-mTOR, MAPK and Src-family signalling without erythema or crusting, while oral dosing was inactive (mean reduction 35%; p ≥ 0.2). Phospho-Akt fell in a concentration-dependent manner in human explants, and lead gels delivered epidermal concentrations at or above the IC90 required for pathway inhibition. In the UV-B-irradiated SKH-1 model, topical bimiralisib prevented cSCC occurrence and Ki-67 labelling but did not reduce atypia in AKs or SCCIS. Conclusions: Activity is governed by epidermal drug exposure rather than intrinsic potency, supporting topical dual PI3K-mTOR inhibition as a non-inflammatory field-directed strategy for AK.

item.title: Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma: An Updated Review on: Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Treatment Strategies.
item.dc:creator: Al-Abbadi MA, Abuawad HZ, Abdelrahim B, Hyassat D, Al-Muqbel K, Alabbadi AM, Younes NA
item.description:
Authors: Al-Abbadi MA, Abuawad HZ, Abdelrahim B, Hyassat D, Al-Muqbel K, Alabbadi AM, Younes NA
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223628
Published: 2026-Nov-13
PMID: 43088158



Abstract:
We aim to provide a focused update on the pathogenesis, various diagnostic triaging processes, and the comprehensive treatment modalities of differentiated thyroid carcinoma. PubMed and Google Scholar databases/search engines were utilized using pertinent keywords. We prioritized recent articles from the American Thyroid Association. The diagnostic modalities span imaging features, pre-operative fine-needle aspiration, molecular and genetic analyses on these aspirates and the histopathological evaluation of resected thyroid tissue. The management protocols are variable, including surgery, radioactive iodine therapy and medical management as adjuvant treatment options. The sequence and intensity of these treatments vary and are currently dynamic. The triaging approach differs and depends on assessment of multiple risk factors of these carcinomas. This review presents recent advances in diagnostic modalities, including molecular and genetic alterations, followed by surgical, radioiodine, and targeted medical therapies. It also addresses the current standard of care and discusses the "dynamic" decision-making process. In conclusion, DTC diagnosis and management exhibited significant changes in the last two decades. Preoperative assessment by aspiration cytology is well recognized and has become standardized with evidence-based risk of malignancy assessment, and consequently triage recommendations accordingly. The spectrum of molecular and genetic signature changes of DTC is expanding and becoming available to evaluate in the preoperative evaluation phase. We review and summarize the recent consensus guidelines for surgical, radioactive iodine and medical management of DTC. We offer a discussion on the recent "dynamic risk assessment" concept as well as its relationship with the aforementioned treatment modalities.

item.title: Three-Dimensional Imaging, Printing, and Augmented Reality in Surgical Oncology: A Descriptive Implementation Framework at a Comprehensive Cancer Center.
item.dc:creator: Oudeh A, Kim HH, Michael S, Jen JW, Frydenlund N, Cho JS, Patel T, Kaza S, Gerstle JT, Behr G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Oudeh A, Kim HH, Michael S, Jen JW, Frydenlund N, Cho JS, Patel T, Kaza S, Gerstle JT, Behr G, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223627
Published: 2026-Nov-13
PMID: 43088157



Abstract:
Background: Three-dimensional (3D) visualization of radiological imaging has emerged as a valuable tool in surgical oncology, with applications spanning diagnostics, perioperative planning, intraoperative guidance, and patient communication. Despite its growing clinical relevance, integration into routine surgical workflows remains inconsistent and poorly standardized across specialties. Methods: We describe select cases illustrating a multispecialty feasibility and implementation experience evaluating the integration of 3D reconstruction, 3D printing, and augmented reality into surgical oncology workflows across a comprehensive cancer center. Describing cases and series of interest, we demonstrate how a structured implementation workflow was applied covering image acquisition, segmentation, volumetric rendering, and modality selection based on the specific clinical problem. A feasibility framework is proposed in terms of workflow integration, modality-to-problem fit, and clinical utility as described by the operating team. Results: Seven select case groups spanning pediatric, head and neck, urologic, gynecologic, and thoracic surgical oncology were included, with group sizes ranging from 1 to 14 patients. In 3 patients with hepatoblastoma, 3D printed anatomical models were successfully integrated into patient and family education consultations to convey tumor extent and the scope of planned resection. Segmentation-based visualization was implemented for preoperative planning in 2 patients with skull base malignancies, with the 3D workflow described as useful for operative planning by the operating team in both cases. Augmented reality (AR)-assisted 3D reconstruction was incorporated into the planning workflow for 3 patients undergoing robotic partial nephrectomy for complex renal tumors, facilitating review of vascular anatomy and assessment of the feasibility of nephron-sparing surgery. In 2 patients with suspected advanced ovarian cancer, volumetric rendering with AR was integrated into preoperative resectability planning. Among 14 patients undergoing chest wall tumor resection, patient-specific 3D printed ribcage replicas were used for preoperative implant preparation. In a separate cohort of 2 chest wall patients, AR visualization was used for spatial surgical planning. Conclusions: Across diverse oncologic contexts and surgical specialties, 3D reconstruction, printing, and augmented reality were successfully integrated into existing perioperative workflows, with each modality selected based on the specific clinical problem at hand. This experience describes a structured, modality-matched implementation framework that may serve as a practical starting point for institutions seeking to incorporate these technologies. Prospective, controlled studies are needed to establish independent clinical benefit. Broader adoption will require standardized selection criteria, prospective evaluation, and workflow adaptation for centers beyond high-volume academic institutions.

item.title: Is vaping already old news? Patterns and risk factors of oral nicotine product use among adolescents from a German school-based study.
item.dc:creator: Heinz A, Penner L, Graf F, Heitmann N, Drömann D, Brinkmann F, Franzen KF, Lüthgen M
item.description:
Authors: Heinz A, Penner L, Graf F, Heitmann N, Drömann D, Brinkmann F, Franzen KF, Lüthgen M
Journal: BMC public health | DOI: 10.1186/s12889-026-30334-8
Published: 2026-Nov-13
PMID: 43073892



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral nicotine products such as nicotine pouches and tobacco pouches (snus) have gained increasing popularity among adolescents. However, data on their use and associated factors among adolescents in Germany remain limited. METHODS: A cross-sectional school-based study was conducted in 2026 within the prevention project *School*Vape*Science*. A total of 958 adolescents aged 11 to 21 years completed an anonymous digital questionnaire assessing oral nicotine use, risk perception, social and parental influences, social media exposure, motives for use, and adverse effects. Group differences and hierarchical multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. RESULTS: Overall, 9.4% of adolescents reported lifetime use of nicotine pouches or tobacco pouches (snus). Regular use of oral nicotine products was more common among male adolescents than among female adolescents. Increasing age was associated with higher odds of oral nicotine use (OR = 1.61; 95% CI [1.28, 2.03]; p < .001). The strongest association was observed for nicotine use within the social environment (OR = 7.21; 95% CI [3.23, 16.08]; p < .001). Adolescents perceiving oral nicotine products as less harmful than cigarettes were more likely to report personal use (OR = 2.22; 95% CI [1.05, 4.67]; p = .037). Adolescents with oral nicotine use also reported greater exposure to oral-nicotine-related social media content, including advertising, influencer content, and memes. Frequently reported adverse effects included burning sensations in the mouth, dizziness, nausea, headaches, and tachycardia. CONCLUSIONS: Oral nicotine products were already used by a relevant proportion of adolescents participating in this German school-based study. Social influences and reduced risk perception appear to play important roles in adolescent use, while social media may contribute to the visibility and normalization of these products. Although oral nicotine product use remains less common than smoking and e-cigarette use, preventive and regulatory strategies should address these products alongside conventional nicotine products.

item.title: Few-Shot Prototype Adaptation of Frozen Pathology Foundation Models for Cross-Tissue and Cross-Cancer Transfer: From Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma to Breast Cancer Lymph Node Metastases.
item.dc:creator: Sumon RI, Akter S, Mozumder AQ, Ali Al-Onaizan MH, Chelloug SA, Muthanna M
item.description:
Authors: Sumon RI, Akter S, Mozumder AQ, Ali Al-Onaizan MH, Chelloug SA, Muthanna M
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223624
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43088154



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Deep networks trained to recognise oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) in histopathology perform well on held-out images from the same collections, but a recent study found that such a network lost most of its discriminative ability on lymph node tissue. We examined whether encoder fine-tuning or label-free adaptation changes this, and how many labelled target patches are needed to recover performance. Methods: The source domain comprised 23,290 images of oral and oropharyngeal mucosa from three public collections. The target domain was PatchCamelyon, a public dataset of sentinel lymph node patches from breast cancer patients; its metastases are breast carcinoma, so the transfer crosses both tissue type and cancer histology. We used 40,000 target patches from 216 slides, split into slide-disjoint adaptation and evaluation pools. We compared nine encoders in ten configurations, including three pathology foundation models (Phikon, Phikon-v2 and the recent Midnight model). We evaluated direct transfer with frozen and fine-tuned encoders, label-free adaptation, and few-shot adaptation, in which we compute class prototypes from k labelled target patches using a frozen encoder. All results are at patch level. Results: Direct transfer failed for every configuration (external AUROC 0.35-0.64), including fine-tuned networks (mean over three seeds 0.44-0.52) and fine-tuned Phikon (0.54-0.58). Label-free methods did not close the gap; a zero-shot vision-language model reached 0.77. With a frozen Phikon encoder, prototypes from 10 and 50 labelled patches per class reached 0.869 ± 0.056 and 0.930 ± 0.015, against 0.82-0.86 at 50 patches for encoders without histology pre-training and 0.977 for a classifier trained on 20,000 labelled patches. Logistic regression on the same patches performed similarly at one and two patches per class and better from five upward (0.955 at 50). Midnight reached 0.922 with prototypes at 50 patches per class, similar to Phikon. The results were similar when support and evaluation patches came from different scanning centres. Conclusions: For the methods and datasets evaluated, no classifier trained on oral tissue transferred to this cross-tissue, cross-cancer target. Our analyses suggest that the change in what the classes contain mattered more than stain or scale, but they do not separate the causal contributions of tissue, cancer histology and acquisition. Frozen pathology foundation models made label-efficient classification on the target domain inexpensive; this replaces the oral-trained classifier and does not use oral images. The findings concern patch-level classification of breast cancer metastases and do not establish clinical performance for OSCC lymph node metastases.

item.title: Risk-Based Triage of Women with Persistent HR-HPV Positivity at 12-Month Recall in Cervical Cancer Screening: A Multicenter Retrospective Evaluation of Cytology and Partial HPV Genotyping.
item.dc:creator: Pompeo G, Mongia A, Paganini I, Gorini G, Puliti D, Pacella S, Fuzzi B, Del Mistro A, Frayle H, Sartori G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Pompeo G, Mongia A, Paganini I, Gorini G, Puliti D, Pacella S, Fuzzi B, Del Mistro A, Frayle H, Sartori G, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223621
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43088150



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Under the current Italian HPV-based cervical screening protocol, women with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) positivity at the 12-month recall are referred to colposcopy regardless of cytology results. Although this strategy maximizes lesion detection, it may result in a high number of colposcopies, most of which do not identify CIN2+. We evaluated whether partial HPV genotyping combined with cytology can improve risk stratification in women with persistent HPV positivity at the 12-month recall. METHODS: A multicenter retrospective analysis of cervical screening data collected from four Italian screening programs (Florence, Padua, Umbria and Emilia Romagna) was performed. Among the 270,714 women screened between 2015 and 2019 (2016-2018 in Florence), 4589 women with persistent HR-HPV positivity at 12-month recall after baseline HPV-positive/NILM (negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy) results were included. Four alternative triage strategies based on cytology and HPV 16/18 genotyping were retrospectively simulated and compared with the current protocol. Outcomes included CIN2 (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2) or worse (CIN2+) detection, relative sensitivity for CIN2+ and CIN3 (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3) or worse (CIN3+), positive predictive value (PPV) and reduction in colposcopy referrals. RESULTS: Under the current protocol, 4589 colposcopies identified 327 CIN2+ lesions, including 113 CIN3+ lesions, yielding a PPV for CIN2+ of 7.1%. Overall, 36.7% of CIN2+ lesions were associated with NILM cytology at recall. HPV 16/18 genotyping identified 43.3% of these cytologically occult lesions. In this retrospective simulation, among the evaluated strategies, referral of HPV 16/18-positive women regardless of cytology and referral of women with low-grade or worse cytology regardless of genotype would have achieved the most favorable balance between sensitivity and efficiency. This approach would have reduced colposcopy referrals by 57.7% (95% CI, 56.3-59.2), nearly doubled the PPV for CIN2+ to 13.4% (95% CI, 11.9-14.9) and maintained relative sensitivities of 79.2% (95% CI, 74.5-83.3) for CIN2+ and 85.0% (95% CI, 77.2-90.4) for CIN3+. Performance varied across centers, with imprecise center-specific estimates (relative CIN3+ sensitivity of Strategy 2 from 62.5% in Emilia Romagna to 91.1% in Umbria), so generalizability should be assessed cautiously. CONCLUSIONS: Combining partial HPV genotyping with cytology would have substantially improved risk stratification in women with persistent HR-HPV positivity at 12-month recall. In this retrospective simulation, a risk-based approach would have substantially reduced immediate colposcopies while maintaining a relative sensitivity for CIN3+ of 85.0%. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support prospective evaluation of integrating molecular and cytological information into 12-month recall management.

item.title: Tumor Origin, Cavernous Sinus Invasion, and Extent of Resection in Sphenoid Wing Meningiomas: A Single-Center Experience.
item.dc:creator: Drewes NB, Jain R, Koutah L, Nandoliya KR, Drake W, Congivaram HTS, Sanchez-Forteza A, Garovich M, Bobat A, Delfino KR, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Drewes NB, Jain R, Koutah L, Nandoliya KR, Drake W, Congivaram HTS, Sanchez-Forteza A, Garovich M, Bobat A, Delfino KR, et al.
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223619
Published: 2026-Nov-12
PMID: 43088149



Abstract:
Background/Objectives: Sphenoid wing meningiomas are skull base meningiomas whose resection is often complicated by involvement of the optic canal, cavernous sinus, orbit, and internal carotid artery. However, prior studies use heterogeneous classification systems that may conflate tumor site of origin with patterns of extension, making comparisons by location difficult. We evaluated sphenoid wing meningiomas using an origin-based classification to assess differences in extent of resection according to tumor origin and cavernous sinus invasion. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 39 patients who underwent resection of histopathologically confirmed sphenoid wing meningiomas at a single center between 2010 and 2024. Tumors were classified as medial or lateral according to their dominant dural attachment on MRI. An exploratory stratified analysis compared GTR rates between medial and lateral tumors according to cavernous sinus invasion status. Results: GTR was achieved in 4 of 15 medial tumors (26.7%) and 18 of 24 lateral tumors (75.0%; p = 0.007). Cavernous sinus invasion occurred in 9 of 15 medial and 2 of 24 lateral tumors. Among tumors without cavernous sinus invasion, GTR was achieved in 4 of 6 medial and 18 of 22 lateral tumors (66.7% vs. 81.8%; p = 0.58). All six events were progression after STR, with no recurrence after GTR. The 1-year recurrence-free survival after GTR and progression-free survival after less-than-GTR were 100% and 73.9%, respectively (p = 0.005). Conclusions: Medial sphenoid wing meningiomas more often involve critical skull base structures and are less likely to undergo GTR. The smaller observed difference among non-invaded tumors is hypothesis-generating because this subgroup only comprised six medial tumors.

item.title: Knockdown of STAT1 inhibits epithelial-mesenchymal transition and attenuates the migration of nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells.
item.dc:creator: Qiao F, Lu J, Han Y, Zhang Y, Yang L, Huang S
item.description:
Authors: Qiao F, Lu J, Han Y, Zhang Y, Yang L, Huang S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1993363
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43094494



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the expression pattern and functional role of signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), focusing on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and cellular motility. METHODS: High-throughput RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of 4 NPC and 3 non-cancerous nasopharyngeal tissues identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses. STAT1 in situ expression was verified by immunohistochemistry (IHC) in paired clinical specimens. Stable STAT1-knockdown models were established in human 6-10B NPC cells using lentiviral shRNAs, with silencing efficiency confirmed via Western blotting. Protein levels of core EMT markers (N-cadherin, Snail, Vimentin, β-catenin, α-SMA, and E-cadherin) were evaluated, and two-dimensional cellular motility was assessed using real-time scratch wound healing assays (0-96 h). RESULTS: Transcriptomic profiling revealed 6,394 DEGs significantly enriched in cell adhesion and junction remodeling pathways. IHC confirmed prominent cytoplasmic and nuclear STAT1 overexpression in NPC tissues. Western blotting verified potent STAT1 knockdown (sh1: ~52.0% of NC, P< 0.05). STAT1 silencing significantly downregulated mesenchymal markers-including N-cadherin (P< 0.001), Snail (P< 0.0001), Vimentin (P< 0.01), β-catenin (P< 0.001), and α-SMA (P< 0.001)-without altering epithelial E-cadherin levels (P > 0.05). Consistently, STAT1 depletion markedly decelerated wound closure rates across 24 to 96 h compared to Mock controls (P< 0.05 or P< 0.01). CONCLUSION: STAT1 is aberrantly overexpressed in NPC. Targeting STAT1 attenuates mesenchymal phenotypic traits, EMT-associated molecular programs, and cell motility, identifying STAT1 as a candidate molecular vulnerability that warrants further preclinical evaluation.

item.title: Robotic Bilateral Total Thyroidectomy Using the Double Bipolar Method with the da Vinci SP System: A Propensity Score-Matched Comparison with the Xi System.
item.dc:creator: Kang S, Kim DW, Ryu JS, Lee SW, Kim E, Kim JK, Kang SW, Jeong JJ, Nam KH, Chung W
item.description:
Authors: Kang S, Kim DW, Ryu JS, Lee SW, Kim E, Kim JK, Kang SW, Jeong JJ, Nam KH, Chung W
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223609
Published: 2026-Nov-11
PMID: 43088137



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The da Vinci SP system offers a single-port configuration with flexible, multijointed instruments, but evidence comparing it with the Xi system in robotic bilateral total thyroidectomy (BTT) remains limited. This study compared surgical outcomes and postoperative complications between the two platforms. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 548 consecutive patients with thyroid cancer who underwent robotic BTT by a single surgeon between 2010 and 2024. Patients were analyzed separately according to central compartment neck dissection (CCND) or modified radical neck dissection (MRND). Propensity score matching was performed at a 1:1 ratio based on age, sex, body mass index, and tumor size. Serial calcium and parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels were additionally examined in matched patients who developed transient hypocalcemia. RESULTS: The overall cohort included 396 patients in the Xi group and 152 in the SP group. Overall complications (34.3% vs. 21.7%, p = 0.003) and transient hypocalcemia (28.3% vs. 14.5%, p = 0.001) were less frequent in the SP group. Propensity score matching yielded 70 pairs in the CCND cohort and 47 pairs in the MRND cohort. In the matched CCND cohort, the SP group had lower rates of overall complications (18.6% vs. 40.0%, p = 0.024) and transient hypocalcemia (10.0% vs. 30.0%, p = 0.013). Complication rates did not differ significantly between the platforms in the matched MRND cohort. Surgical and pathological outcomes were generally comparable. Among patients with transient hypocalcemia, the decline in calcium at 6 months was smaller in the SP group in the CCND cohort (p = 0.013), whereas the MRND cohort showed smaller declines in PTH at selected postoperative time points but no significant between-group differences in calcium changes. CONCLUSION: Robotic BTT using the da Vinci SP system and the Double Bipolar Method was safe and feasible. Compared with the Xi system, this approach achieved generally comparable surgical and pathological outcomes and was associated with fewer postoperative complications in the matched CCND cohort.

item.title: Impact of Second Primary Cancers on Treatment Modifications in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Head and Neck Cancer Referred for Curative-Intent Radiotherapy: A Retrospective Study.

Published: 2026-Nov-11

Abstract:
Objective: Development of second primary cancers (SPCs) is a significant risk for head and neck cancer (HNC) patients. This study investigates the impact of synchronous and metachronous SPCs on treatment strategies of newly diagnosed HNC. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed patients referred for curative-intent radiotherapy between 2022 and 2024. The primary outcome was the impact of SPCs on HNC (chemo)radiotherapy strategies, with SPC prevalence and distribution as secondary outcomes. Results: A total of 285 patients were included. In 28.4% an SPC was observed. A total of 8.4% had a synchronous malignancy, 16.5% were treated for another malignancy in the past and 3.5% presented with both a synchronous and metachronous cancer. The treatment was impacted in 37.0% of patients with an SPC. Treatment modifications included altered radiotherapy field (23.5%), treatment delays (13.6%), adjusted radio- or chemotherapy regimens (2.5% each), and transition to palliative care (1.2%). Conclusion: A substantial proportion of SPCs influenced the radiotherapy (RT) management in all domains. The complexity of treatment was further increased by the need for additional pre-treatment evaluations and consideration of prior therapies.

item.title: Osteomyelitis Following Mandibular Third Molar Extraction: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Clinical and Radiographic Characteristics and Time to Resolution.
item.dc:creator: Lee DY, Shim GJ
item.description:
Authors: Lee DY, Shim GJ

Published: 2026-Nov-11
PMID: 43085427



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteomyelitis after mandibular third molar extraction is a rare but serious complication that may require prolonged treatment and additional surgical intervention. However, its clinical and radiographic characteristics and factors associated with time to resolution remain poorly defined. PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to estimate the time to resolution and identify factors associated with resolution among patients who developed osteomyelitis after mandibular third molar extraction. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE: This retrospective cohort study was conducted at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Kyungpook National University Dental Hospital. Patients diagnosed with osteomyelitis after mandibular third molar extraction and treated between January 2020 and September 2025 were included. Patients with pre-existing odontogenic infection or osteomyelitis, a history of antiresorptive, antiangiogenic or immunosuppressive medication use, or prior head and neck radiation therapy were excluded. PREDICTOR VARIABLES: The predictor variable was a set of heterogenous factors categorized as demographic, clinical, radiographic, and treatment-related factors. MAIN OUTCOME VARIABLE: The primary outcome was time to resolution, defined as the time from symptom onset to complete clinical resolution of osteomyelitis, with resolution defined as the absence of clinical signs and symptoms of infection. COVARIATES: Not applicable. ANALYSES: Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was used to estimate time to resolution. Univariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were performed. Statistical significance was set at P < .05. RESULTS: The sample was composed of 16 subjects with a mean age of 47.0 ± 14.5 years, and 12 (75.0%) were male. The median of time to resolution was 11.0 weeks (interquartile range: 5.8 to 12.8) and the median follow-up duration was 8.5 months (interquartile range: 6.0 to 14.5). Sequestrectomy was associated with a shorter time to resolution compared with curettage (hazard ratio: 3.7; 95% CI: 1.1 to 12.3; P = .03). No statistically significant associations were identified for the other variables. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The median time to resolution of osteomyelitis following mandibular third molar extraction was 11.0 weeks. Sequestrectomy was associated with a shorter time to resolution, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and potential confounding by treatment selection.

item.title: Selecting the Optimal Margin: Early Multidisciplinary Coordination Can Reduce Surgical Morbidity in Merkel Cell Carcinoma Management.
item.dc:creator: Wilk V, Ouellette S, Bouché N, Chen B, Fu A, Nghiem P, Byrd D, Jackson KM
item.description:
Authors: Wilk V, Ouellette S, Bouché N, Chen B, Fu A, Nghiem P, Byrd D, Jackson KM
Journal: Cancers | DOI: 10.3390/cancers18223596
Published: 2026-Nov-10
PMID: 43088126



Abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare, aggressive, cutaneous neuroendocrine cancer that requires multidisciplinary coordination to optimize patient outcomes. However, surgical decision-making still commonly occurs in isolation prior to multidisciplinary discussion, which may increase the risk of avoidable surgical morbidity. METHODS: We performed a retrospective institutional review of five illustrative cases of pathologically confirmed MCC. Cases were selected to illustrate specific challenges associated with early surgical intervention without prior multidisciplinary decision-making. RESULTS: Across the five cases, wide local excision was associated with significant morbidity, functional loss, and delays in adjuvant radiation therapy (RT) that may have been reducible through earlier multidisciplinary coordination. Several cases highlight that wider margins alone did not clearly improve locoregional control, with recurrences occurring beyond pathologically negative margins. CONCLUSIONS: These cases illustrate how surgical planning in isolation may increase morbidity and delay timely adjuvant RT without clearly improving oncologic outcomes. Early multidisciplinary discussion prior to definitive excision may permit narrower guideline-consistent margins, timely adjuvant RT, and improved functional and cosmetic outcomes. Multimodal treatment planning should be considered a cornerstone of MCC management.

item.title: Therapeutic HPV vaccines for PD-1 blockade-resistant HPV-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: mechanistic rationale, clinical limitations, and biomarker-guided combinations.
item.dc:creator: Hu Y, Li Z, Liu H, Wen B
item.description:
Authors: Hu Y, Li Z, Liu H, Wen B
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1953732
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43080483



Abstract:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a common malignancy that continues to present substantial therapeutic challenges despite decades of research. Immune checkpoint blockade agents targeting the programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) axis have emerged as a frontline therapeutic modality for patients with recurrent/metastatic disease. However, suboptimal objective response rates and pervasive inherent and acquired resistance mechanisms significantly limit clinical efficacy. Notably, the escalating incidence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven HNSCC, particularly oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), has necessitated novel treatment paradigms. The HPV-encoded oncoviral antigens represent optimal targets for precision immunotherapeutic interventions. Here, we summarize the multifactorial mechanisms underlying resistance to PD-1 blockade in HNSCC and discuss how therapeutic HPV vaccines may restore antitumor immune responses by remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and expanding virus-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes. These findings support the biological rationale for combining therapeutic HPV vaccines with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade; however, this strategy should still be regarded as investigational because clinical benefit has not been consistently demonstrated in randomized studies. In addition, we review recent preclinical and translational advances, compare major vaccine delivery platforms, and discuss future research directions and challenges in this evolving field. Finally, we advance a working hypothesis that therapeutic efficacy is contingent upon three biological prerequisites-intact MHC-I antigen presentation, baseline PD-L1 expression, and the absence of dominant non-PD-1 immunosuppressive barriers-and discuss the implications of this precision-enrichment framework for future trial design.

item.title: Surgery during regorafenib therapy in children, adolescents, and young adults with bone sarcomas: perioperative management and feasibility.
item.dc:creator: Zelwiańska A, Bilska K, Koziński T, Walenta T, Malesza I, Szymborska A, Bronowicki K, Pachuta B, Jasica W, Antoniuk-Majchrzak J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zelwiańska A, Bilska K, Koziński T, Walenta T, Malesza I, Szymborska A, Bronowicki K, Pachuta B, Jasica W, Antoniuk-Majchrzak J, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1834965
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43080320



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Regorafenib is an oral multikinase inhibitor with documented activity in relapsed and metastatic bone sarcomas, but data on its perioperative management in children, adolescents, and young adults are scarce. Given its antiangiogenic mechanism and potential impact on wound healing and bleeding risk, defining safe perioperative strategies is essential when surgery is required during ongoing treatment. METHODS: This retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from the REGBONE clinical trial at the Institute of Mother and Child included children, adolescents, and young adults with relapsed or metastatic osteosarcoma or Ewing sarcoma who received regorafenib and underwent at least one surgical procedure between April 2022 and December 2025. The parent trial enrolled patients aged 9-21 years. Perioperative management involved temporary regorafenib interruption and individualized postoperative resumption guided by predefined wound-healing criteria. The data cutoff was January 30, 2026. RESULTS: Fourteen patients underwent 18 surgical procedures across 14 regorafenib interruption episodes. The median age at surgery was 16.2 years [IQR 12.8-18.0]; most had osteosarcoma (93%). Thoracic procedures accounted for 67% of surgeries. The median from the last regorafenib dose to the first procedure was 17 days [IQR 11-22]. Regorafenib was resumed after 12 of 14 interruption episodes (86%), with a median of 32 days [IQR 22-48] from the final procedure to resumption. The median total treatment interruption was 67 days [IQR 46-91]. Postoperative complications within 30 days were recorded in two patients (14%; 95% CI 2%-43%), both managed conservatively without surgical reintervention or therapeutic antibiotics; regorafenib was resumed after 70 and 124 days, respectively. No perioperative or 30-day deaths were recorded among 14 patients, and no 90-day deaths occurred among 13 evaluable patients. Among 13 patients with planned postoperative chemotherapy, systemic treatment was resumed within 14 days in all cases (median 9 days, IQR 8-10). The median OS from surgery was 29.6 months (95% CI 12.2-not reached), and the 12-month OS rate was 84.6% (95% CI 51.2%-95.9%). CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that surgery during a regorafenib treatment course is feasible in selected children, adolescents, and young adults when treatment interruption is individualized and resumption is guided by clinical wound healing. Early postoperative chemotherapy administration was also feasible in patients for whom it was planned. However, the small cohort and prolonged treatment interruptions limit conclusions regarding safety. Larger multicenter studies are needed to inform perioperative management recommendations.

item.title: Radiation-induced fibrosis in head and neck cancer survivors: long-term sequelae and multimodal management.
item.dc:creator: Mohanty A, Glover H, Abdi S, Fuller CD, Huh B, Javed S
item.description:
Authors: Mohanty A, Glover H, Abdi S, Fuller CD, Huh B, Javed S
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1981918
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43075164



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Improved survival in head and neck cancer has increased the number of patients living with late effects of treatment, among which radiation-induced fibrosis is a progressive and often irreversible complication with important consequences for pain, function, and quality of life. In addition to contributing to trismus, dysphagia, speech impairment, and reduced cervical mobility, fibrosis has important implications for airway management and perioperative care. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes current clinical and translational literature on radiation-induced fibrosis in head and neck cancer survivorship, with emphasis on its epidemiology, underlying mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, prevention, management, emerging therapies, and multidisciplinary care, while highlighting functional outcomes and anesthesia-relevant airway sequelae. RESULTS: Radiation-induced fibrosis may emerge months to years after treatment and is driven by persistent inflammatory and profibrotic signaling that promotes tissue remodeling and long-term dysfunction. Risk is influenced by patient and treatment factors including smoking, concurrent chemoradiotherapy, radiation dose and field design, surgical dissection, and baseline functional impairment. Clinically, fibrosis contributes to restricted neck motion, trismus, dysphagia, aspiration risk, dysphonia, chronic pain, and psychosocial burden. Current management is largely multimodal and supportive, centering on rehabilitation, speech and swallow therapy, symptomatic pharmacological treatment, interventional pain procedures, and selective surgery. Emerging strategies, such as antifibrotic agents, mesenchymal stromal cell therapies, hyperbaric oxygen, and candidate biomarker strategies, remain investigational but may expand future treatment options. DISCUSSION: Radiation-induced fibrosis is an underrecognized survivorship challenge that extends beyond tissue scarring to long-term dysfunctions across airway, swallowing, pain, and quality of life domains. Future progress will depend on standardized diagnostic criteria, earlier detection, prevention-focused trials, continued evaluation of investigational therapies, and patient-centered outcomes that better capture the lived burden of survivors and guide more precise supportive care.

item.title: Lifestyle-associated hyperglycemia and aberrant TSH glycoforms in aggressive thyroid carcinoma: glycosylation-mediated mechanisms in treatment resistance hyperglycemia, TSH glycoforms & thyroid cancer.
item.dc:creator: P R A, Kamal MV, Joshi K, Jagadish C, Jamadar S, Tiwari P
item.description:
Authors: P R A, Kamal MV, Joshi K, Jagadish C, Jamadar S, Tiwari P
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1968674
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43075113



Abstract:
This review examines the critical intersection between lifestyle-associated hyperglycemia and aggressive thyroid carcinoma, with a particular focus on the role of aberrant thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) glycosylation. Chronic hyperglycemia, a characteristic of metabolic disorders such as type 2 diabetes, contributes to a pro-oxidative and pro-inflammatory tumor microenvironment. We propose that this metabolic stress enhances the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway, which may result in abnormal structural remodeling of TSH, specifically hypersialylation and increased N-glycan branching. We hypothesize that these altered TSH glycoforms dynamically interact with the TSH receptor. Due to their prolonged circulatory half-life, they may redirect canonical signaling toward sustained, atypical modulation of oncogenic networks, notably the PI3K/Akt/mTOR and MAPK pathways. These proposed signaling alterations could potentially contribute to tumor cell proliferation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, immune evasion, and potential resistance to multimodal therapies in advanced thyroid carcinomas. These glycomic alterations may represent potential biomarker candidates; however, their diagnostic and prognostic utility remains clinically unvalidated. These findings provide a rationale for investigating whether metabolic regulation and glycosylation-targeted approaches could contribute to future strategies for overcoming treatment resistance in aggressive thyroid carcinomas.

Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
PURPOSE: To establish a risk-stratified management framework for cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) by integrating AJCC 9th edition staging, the 2024 HNCIG extranodal extension (ENE) consensus, AI radiomics, and modern immunotherapy, with critical appraisal of clinical utility and external validation. METHODS: A PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review of 49 high-quality studies identified through database search (January 2019-April 30, 2025), with 3 additional post-cutoff studies used for background context; stratified quality assessment was performed using RoB 2, NOS, AMSTAR 2, and QUADAS-2. FINDING: Unified pathological-radiological ENE criteria were consolidated for HNSCC; AI radiomics showed promising but insufficiently externally validated performance for occult metastasis prediction; risk-adapted algorithms integrating selective neck dissection, adjuvant anti-PD-1 immunotherapy, and de-escalation were constructed for specific risk strata. CONCLUSION: This review provides a risk-stratified evidence synthesis for LNM management in HNSCC, while highlighting that radiomics models require prospective multicenter validation before clinical deployment, and that management recommendations should be applied within appropriate risk and disease strata.

item.title: Weakly supervised computational pathology for prognostic stratification in locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a multicenter external validation study.
item.dc:creator: Jiang C, Lu W, Ding M, Zhou X, Li B, Liu X
item.description:
Authors: Jiang C, Lu W, Ding M, Zhou X, Li B, Liu X
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1966935
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43074870



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Accurate prognostic stratification remains challenging in locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC), as conventional clinicopathological factors provide limited precision for individualized risk assessment. Although hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) contain abundant morphological information, their prognostic potential in LA-NPC remains underexplored using computational pathology approaches. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Patients with stage III-IVA LA-NPC from three Chinese tertiary centers were allocated into a training cohort, an internal validation cohort, and an independent external test cohort. A CLAM-inspired attention-based multiple-instance learning (MIL) model was developed using pretreatment H&E-stained WSIs and externally validated. The model was compared with four alternative MIL architectures incorporating different feature extractors and pooling strategies. Prognostic performance for 3-year progression-free survival (PFS) was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, the concordance index (C-index), Kaplan-Meier analysis, decision curve analysis, and Cox regression. RESULTS: A total of 253 patients contributing 265 WSIs were included: 149 patients/160 WSIs in the training cohort, 52 patients/53 WSIs in the internal validation cohort, and 52 patients/52 WSIs in the independent external test cohort. In the internal validation cohort, the CLAM-inspired Attention MIL model yielded an AUC of 0.883 (95% CI, 0.762-0.969) and a C-index of 0.802 (95% CI, 0.705-0.884) for predicting 3-year PFS. In the external test cohort, the model achieved an AUC of 0.721 (95% CI, 0.573-0.849) and a C-index of 0.710 (95% CI, 0.591-0.819). The model significantly stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups in both cohorts and showed numerically higher AUC and C-index estimates than the four comparative MIL architectures. The risk score was linked to an elevated risk of progression (HR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.06-1.60; P = 0.0126). CONCLUSIONS: A weakly supervised CLAM-inspired Attention MIL framework can extract prognostically relevant information from routine H&E-stained WSIs and provide externally validated risk stratification for patients with LA-NPC. This approach may complement conventional clinicopathological assessment and facilitate individualized prognostic evaluation in precision oncology.

item.title: Reconstruction with a novel pedicled mucoperiosteal hinge flap and dura suturing: a new minimally invasive concept and closure technique for endoscopic endonasal surgery.

Abstract:
OBJECTS: The authors aimed to evaluate their experience with the minimally invasive reconstruction technique using pedicled mucoperiostea hinge flap (PMHF) with dura suturing after EES. Outcomes were compared with those of the traditional reconstruction using the NSF. METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 33 consecutive patients who underwent EES for pituitary adenoma resection. All these 33 patients were reconstructed with pedicled mucoperiosteal hinge flap with dura suturing and were compared with 32 consecutive patients treated previously using NSF technique. Surgical videos and electronic medical records were reviewed to assess operative times and postoperative outcomes, which were compared between the groups, with a particular focus on nasal function, assessed using the Endoscopic Endonasal Sinus and Skull Base Surgery Questionnaire (EES-Q). RESULTS: Demographics of the two groups were broadly similar. Among the 33 patients using PMHF with dura suturing, the average operative time decreased with experience, showing a trend of improved efficiency. item.title: Ultrastructural features associated with the dot-like cytokeratin pattern in Merkel cell carcinoma: a spectrum of intermediate filament organization.
item.dc:creator: Krotofil M, Maksymowicz M, Owczarek D, Siednienko J, Wawręty W, Rutkowski P, Szumera-Ciećkiewicz A, Donizy P
item.description:
Authors: Krotofil M, Maksymowicz M, Owczarek D, Siednienko J, Wawręty W, Rutkowski P, Szumera-Ciećkiewicz A, Donizy P
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1852807
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43074841



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The characteristic paranuclear "dot-like" immunohistochemical staining pattern is a hallmark of Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC), yet its ultrastructural correlates and potential biological significance remain incompletely defined. METHODS: We analyzed four MCC cases. Three tumors showed a classic paranuclear dot-like staining pattern with cytokeratins (CKAE1/AE3, CK20), while one tumor lacking this pattern served as a control. Ultrastructural evaluation was performed using transmission electron microscopy on FFPE tissue reprocessed for ultrastructural analysis. RESULTS: In all three tumors exhibiting a dot-like cytokeratin pattern, cytokeratin immunoreactivity displayed a morphological spectrum. In some areas, submembranous or linear perinuclear staining predominated and corresponded ultrastructurally to thick bundles of intermediate filaments arranged along the nuclear envelope. Elsewhere, these bundles appeared condensed into compact, dense fibrillar bodies composed of tightly packed, coiled cytokeratin filaments. In additional areas, less dense fibrillar bodies with reduced filament packing were observed. The relative proportion of tumor cells exhibiting each pattern varied among cases. Nuclear envelope invaginations (nuclear pockets) were also identified as an additional ultrastructural feature with variable frequency, forming pseudo-inclusion-like profiles; however, they did not constitute the structural substrate of the dot-like cytokeratin pattern. The control tumor lacked both dot-like cytokeratin expression and fibrillar bodies. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support fibrillar bodies as the primary ultrastructural correlate of the classical dot-like cytokeratin pattern in MCC. The coexistence of thick filament bundles, dense fibrillar bodies, and less dense fibrillar bodies suggests a continuum of intermediate filament reorganization rather than discrete categories. These changes may reflect progressive cytoskeletal remodeling and spatial reorganization with potential links to cellular polarization, motility, and cell division. In contrast, nuclear pockets represent a distinct and unrelated ultrastructural phenomenon. Further functional studies are warranted to clarify the biological significance of these observations.

item.title: Postoperative radiotherapy versus systemic therapy alone for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma following neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Z, Zhao J, Li C, Li Y, Bai Y, Zhang R, Liu C, Liu C
item.description:

Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1978264
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43074770



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (nICT) followed by radical esophagectomy is increasingly used for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), but the incremental value of postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) in patients who also receive postoperative systemic therapy remains uncertain. This study evaluated survival outcomes, recurrence patterns, and treatment-related toxicity associated with adding PORT after nICT and surgery. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 336 patients with LA-ESCC who underwent nICT followed by R0 esophagectomy between February 2021 and November 2024. Postoperatively, 93 patients received systemic therapy plus PORT, whereas 243 received systemic therapy alone. Propensity score matching at a 1:1 ratio was performed to balance baseline clinicopathological characteristics, yielding 71 patients in each group. Disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), recurrence patterns, and treatment-related adverse events were analyzed. RESULTS: After PSM, 142 patients (71 per group) were analyzed. The PORT group demonstrated significantly improved 2-year OS (91.0% vs. 75.5%; HR = 0.409, 95% CI: 0.181-0.925, P = 0.026) and 2-year DFS (74.2% vs. 50.1%; HR = 0.525, 95% CI: 0.303-0.911, P = 0.018) compared to the systemic therapy group. Patients with ypStage III-IV and ypN+ derived the most significant survival benefits. PORT reduced the locoregional recurrence rate from 48.1% to 32.1%, shifting the primary failure mode to distant metastasis (46.4%). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 18.3% of PORT patients (primarily hematologic), with grade 3 radiation esophagitis occurring in only 1.1%. CONCLUSION: For LA-ESCC patients treated with nICT and surgery, adding PORT to postoperative systemic therapy improves survival and optimizes recurrence patterns with acceptable toxicity. It represents a promising intensification strategy for high-risk patients.

item.title: Prospective comparison of CT- and MRI-based tumor delineation based on intraoperative navigation and spatially annotated pathology in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Bauer L, Kühle R, Fuchs J, Moratin J, Deng M, Ehle M, Schindehütte R, Schröter P, Stritzke F, Kozyra K, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bauer L, Kühle R, Fuchs J, Moratin J, Deng M, Ehle M, Schindehütte R, Schröter P, Stritzke F, Kozyra K, et al.
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1884392
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43065419



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Precise tumor delineation is critical for navigation-guided surgery and radiotherapy (RT) in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are both recommended for staging and provide complementary information. However, quantitative comparisons of CT- and MRI-based tumor contours remain scarce, while a spatial comparison with histopathological data has never been performed. Therefore, we prospectively compared gross tumor volumes (GTV) derived from CT and MRI before navigation-guided surgery and correlated the results with spatially annotated pathology. METHODS: This imaging sub-analysis was conducted within the prospective NAVIGATORR trial (NCT05671458). Fifteen patients with locally advanced midfacial SCC underwent contrast-enhanced CT and 1.5T or 3T MRI (T1w, T2w, DWI) for navigation-based surgery planning. Datasets were rigidly co-registered and an experienced radiologist independently contoured the GTV on CT and MRI while blinded to the other modality. Besides qualitative and volumetric evaluation, spatial agreement was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Hausdorff distance (HD). Tumor contours were correlated with spatially annotated intraoperative biopsy locations and histopathological results. RESULTS: Fifteen patients and 109 spatially annotated biopsy locations (19 tumor-positive) were analyzed. MRI was preferred for tumor delineation by the radiologist in all cases, with superior differentiation between tumor and mucosal swelling (73%) and improved soft tissue contrast (67%). MRI based GTVs were significantly larger than CT-based GTVs (median 28.3 ml vs. 16.8 ml; p = 0.02). DSC values demonstrated fair agreement with considerable heterogeneity (median 0.58; IQR 0.47-0.65), and median HD was 16 mm (IQR 12-27 mm). MRI-based contours encompassed numerically more tumor-positive biopsy locations than CT-based contours (6/19 vs. 1/19; clustered McNemar p = 0.20) while including fewer tumor-negative locations (7/90 vs. 10/90; p = 0.53). At patient level, at least one tumor-positive biopsy was located inside the contour in 3/8 (MRI) vs. 1/8 (CT) patients. DISCUSSION: GTV delineation differs substantially between MRI and CT in locally advanced midfacial SCC, and the two modalities provide complementary information. These exploratory findings support the complementary use of MRI and CT for tumor visualization. Clinical implications remain to be shown by the primary endpoint analysis of the NAVIGATORR trial.

Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1878313
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43061359



Abstract:
Cannabis, an ancient plant that has been used for millennia, is increasingly utilized by patients with cancer to alleviate symptoms related to both the disease and its treatment. This complex botanical contains multiple bioactive compounds, most notably delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD), which interact with the endogenous endocannabinoid system. THC has been studied the most, and synthetic cannabinoids are approved for the management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. However, evidence supporting cannabis for other cancer-related symptoms-including chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, insomnia, appetite stimulation, and non-neuropathic pain-remains limited. CBD alone has not demonstrated consistent or meaningful clinical benefit. Although preclinical data exist, there is no clinical evidence supporting cannabis as a cancer treatment. Cannabis may interact with prescribed medications, particularly with high-dose oral formulations, and its effects on immunotherapy are under investigation. Overall, cannabis is generally well tolerated, though adverse effects can be significant. Use is discouraged in individuals under 25 years of age due to ongoing neurodevelopment, and patients with active psychiatric or cardiovascular conditions should use cannabis only under close clinical supervision.

item.title: Association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes after ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Xiao D, Zhou X, Li Q, Xie J
item.description:
Authors: Xiao D, Zhou X, Li Q, Xie J
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1950443
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43060455



Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ileostomy reversal is associated with substantial postoperative morbidity despite being considered a relatively minor surgical procedure. Although glutamine supplementation has been investigated in gastrointestinal surgery, evidence regarding its role in patients undergoing ileostomy reversal remains limited. This study evaluated the association between postoperative glutamine supplementation and short-term outcomes following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with colorectal cancer who underwent elective ileostomy reversal between January 2015 and December 2025. Patients were classified into the glutamine group, who received postoperative intravenous glutamine supplementation, and the control group. Postoperative outcomes within 30 days, including complications, gastrointestinal recovery, and length of hospital stay, were compared between groups. RESULTS: A total of 183 patients were included, comprising 103 patients in the glutamine group and 80 in the control group. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 74 matched pairs were identified. Compared with the control group, the glutamine group had a significantly lower incidence of overall postoperative complications (14.9% vs. 29.7%, P = 0.043) and infectious complications (9.5% vs. 23.0%, P = 0.041). The glutamine group also had shorter times to first flatus, first defecation, and initiation of oral diets, as well as lower incidences of postoperative nausea and vomiting and abdominal distension. Hospital stay was shorter in the glutamine group. No significant between-group differences were observed in postoperative serum prealbumin, total protein, or albumin levels. CONCLUSIONS: In this PSM study, postoperative glutamine supplementation was associated with fewer postoperative complications, faster gastrointestinal recovery, and shorter hospital stay following ileostomy reversal in patients with colorectal cancer. These findings indicate a potential association between glutamine supplementation and favorable short-term postoperative outcomes and warrant confirmation in prospective randomized studies.

item.title: Salivary glands auto-segmentation in head and neck radiotherapy: imaging modalities, models, and clinical relevance.
item.dc:creator: Wong WL, Shum CY, Chow YL, Man KH, Law HKW, Tam SY
item.description:
Authors: Wong WL, Shum CY, Chow YL, Man KH, Law HKW, Tam SY
Journal: Frontiers in oncology | DOI: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1923659
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 43054526



Abstract:
Radiotherapy-induced salivary gland injury is a major contributor to xerostomia and impaired quality of life in patients with head and neck cancer, making accurate organ-at-risk delineation clinically important. Deep learning-based auto-segmentation has the potential to improve contouring efficiency and consistency, but reported performance is heterogeneous and its clinical significance is not always clear. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on salivary gland auto-segmentation across computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PSMA PET-CT), with particular emphasis on gland-specific challenges, performance evaluation, and clinical translation. CT has the largest evidence base and remains most relevant to routine radiotherapy planning, whereas MRI provides improved soft-tissue visualization and PSMA PET-CT offers high functional contrast for selected salivary structures. Across modalities, segmentation performance is generally more challenging for smaller structures, particularly the sublingual and tubarial gland regions. Importantly, geometric metrics such as the Dice similarity coefficient do not alone establish clinical acceptability or dosimetric equivalence; evaluation should also consider boundary accuracy, expert correction burden, clinical acceptability, and dosimetric impact. Current evidence is further limited by heterogeneous study designs and reference standards, scarce external validation, and limited evidence linking auto-segmentation directly to treatment-related toxicity or patient outcomes. Future research should prioritize multi-institutional validation, clinically meaningful evaluation, improved segmentation of small glands, and human-in-the-loop integration into adaptive radiotherapy. Overall, auto-segmentation represents a promising tool for salivary gland delineation, but its clinical implementation should be supported by evidence extending beyond geometric accuracy alone.
